Federal or State highway or major City thoroughfare, the site must be
satisfactorily screened by natural objects, planting, fences or other.
C.   Water Supply: The site shall be at least one thousand feet (1,000') from
any existing well that draws water for human or livestock consumption unless
hydrologic conditions are shown to be such that a greater or lesser distance is
proper. (1985 Code §3-4.0203)
4-5A-4: ZONING AND LAND USE:
The application will be accompanied by a copy of the special use permit issued
for such operation on the site by the City Board of Adjustment.
A.   Present and Proposed Zoning: The plan submitted with the application shall
be accompanied by a map showing all zoning within one thousand feet (1,000')
surrounding the site. The plan shall also indicate the land use proposed for
the site after the filling is completed, although such indication shall not be
binding upon the City.
B.   Comprehensive Plan Land Use: The plan submitted with the application shall
indicate the land use shown for the site area in the future in the
comprehensive plan for the City. (1985 Code §3-4.0204)
4-5A-5: SITE PLAN:
The following particulars shall be included in maps of the site plan, as herein
set forth, and shall accompany the application:
A.   Scale: A map of the disposal site and immediate surroundings, on which a
north arrow and scale of drawing are indicated. Generally, a scale of less than
one inch to one hundred feet (1" = 100') will not be approved.
B.   Boundaries and Markers: The boundaries of the disposal site shall be shown
thereon with sufficient data, including legal description, that a land surveyor
can easily locate the boundary. Natural and manmade monuments indicating the
boundary shall be noted. Where the site is located in an undeveloped area, four
inch (4") boundary markers at least six feet (6') high and painted a bright
color shall be used to identify the boundary so that field inspection teams can
easily identify the site.
C.   Present Contour: Two foot (2') contours of the existing terrain shall be
shown thereon.
D.   Utilities: All existing utilities, including storm and sanitary sewers,
which lead up to or cross the site shall be shown thereon.
E.   Drainage: Existing and future drainage shall be shown thereon along with
any proposed storm sewers.
F.   Drill Holes: The location of the drill holes required by subsection
4-5A-8A shall be shown thereon.
G.   Final Contours: Two foot (2') contours of the final proposed terrain shall
be shown on a separate drawing. (1985 Code §3-4.0205)
4-5A-6: VICINITY MAP:
A map showing the area in the vicinity of the site, which shall be known as the
vicinity map, shall be submitted, of a scale of one inch to six hundred feet
(1"= 600') or less; the area covered by the vicinity map shall be sufficient to
contain the following:
A.   Test Holes: Location of test holes for the monitoring of water quality and
the findings from each.
B.   Streets: Streets and street names, as well as all existing public right of
way on and adjacent to the site.
C.   Fire Hydrants: The nearest fire hydrants. Generally, if there is not a
fire hydrant adjacent to the entrance drive and within three hundred feet
(300') of the active portion of the landfill site, a fire hydrant shall be so
installed and connected with an appropriate extension of the water main. If
covering and compacting is performed daily, or if other equivalent means of
providing fire protection are available, this requirement may be waived by the
Council. (See subsection
4-5A-9D.)
D.   Haul Routes: The haul routes from the nearest City truck route.
E.   Screening: Proposed screening of the site from highways, streets, parks,
and residences and other amenities, as well as the schedule of installation of
such; such screening shall meet the requirements of the Zoning Ordinance and
shall have been demonstrated to and approved by the Board of Adjustment.
F.   Private Wells: All private wells within one thousand feet (1,000') of the
site shall be located and identified thereon.
G.   Occupied Structures: All occupied homes and buildings on the site or
within one thousand feet (1,000') of the boundaries thereof shall be shown,
with their addresses and uses indicated, by color coding or otherwise. (1985
Code §3-4.0206)
4-5A-7: TRAFFIC:
The haul routes shown in the plan shall be reviewed by the Department of Public
Works and City Engineer, or his representative, who shall make recommendations
thereon to the Council. Such haul routes shall be chosen to avoid undue
hardships to residents living adjacent to them and to minimize the likelihood
of premature deterioration of City streets so chosen. (1985 Code §3-4.0207)
4-5A-8: SOILS AND GEOLOGY:
Information as to soil and geological conditions shall be provided as follows:
A.   Geological Cross-Section: The plans shall contain a description of the
drill holes shown on the site plan, which shall be sufficient in number to
prepare geological cross sections of the site, to facilitate a determination of
the acceptability of the site location.
B.   Water Table and Bed Rock: The water table depth and bed rock depth shall
be indicated. If bed rock is excessively deep, it may be estimated.
C.   Soil Report: A soil report shall be provided which indicates the
acceptability of the soil on the site for cover material and the stability of
the slopes after the fill is complete. The vulnerability of the soil
classification to erosion shall also be indicated. (1985 Code §3-4.0208)
4-5A-9: OPERATING SITE:
Plans for site operation, including the following, shall be provided.
A.   Estimated Active Life and Volume: The estimated active life of the site
and the total cubic dimensions of the area to be filled shall be indicated.
B.   Annual and Peak Volume: The volume of construction and demolition material
expected annually and on the peak days shall be indicated.
C.   Cells: The number, size and shape of cells of demolition material shall be
indicated.
D.   Cover: The approximate depth and type of cover material shall be
indicated. The volume of cover material needed for the entire site shall be
indicated as well as the source and soil classification of the cover material
and frequency of covering. Once a week compacting of demolition material and
covering with dirt will be acceptable, provided a bulldozer with a blade,
operator on call, and a stockpile of cover materials are available at all times
on the site in the event of fire. More frequent covering and compacting may be
required by the city if it is deemed necessary to abate a nuisance and shall be
mandatory if the requirements of subsection
4-5A-6C, "Fire Hydrants", of this article are not met.
E.   Gates And Fencing: The times at which the gates will be open as well as
provisions for maintaining the fence at locations required herein shall be
indicated.
F.   Vector Control: The intended continuing vector control, principally rat
abatement and mosquito abatement, shall be indicated.
G.   Personnel And Equipment: The personnel and equipment planned to operate
the site, and the hours and days of the week when they will be on the site,
shall be indicated. (1985 Code §3-4.0209)
4-5A-10: SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL CONTROLS:
Expected environmental impact problems, with specific treatment or controls
intended to eliminate or mitigate negative effects of each, shall be listed.
(1985 Code §3-4.0210)
4-5A-11: INSURANCE:
The applicant shall file a certificate of insurance evidencing the issuance to
the applicant of liability insurance which shall protect the public and any and
all persons from injury which may be sustained by reason of the operation or
condition of the landfill, and that the applicant carries insurance which meets
the requirements of the Iowa workmen's compensation law. Proof of such
insurance shall show a minimum cancellation time of ten (10) days and shall
embody a requirement that the city shall have a right to such notice before
such cancellation can become effective. The proof shall specify evidence of the
following forms of insurance protection.
A.   Operation Liability: Liability insurance covering all operations performed
by the licensed applicant and all persons in the licensed applicant's direct
employment.
B.   Subcontractor: Public liability insurance covering all operations
performed by any subcontractor or independent contractor to whom a portion of
the operations may have been assigned or which in the future may be assigned,
or by any person or legal entity action for or on behalf of the licensed
applicant at or on the site.
C.   Vehicles: Motor vehicle bodily injury insurance and property damage
liability insurance on motor vehicles employed on the site, whether or not
owned by the licensed applicant or by either the subcontractors or independent
contractors under contract to the licensee, or by any other person or legal
entity acting for or on behalf of the licensed applicant at or on the site.
D.   Amount: The main protection shall be insurance coverage with a minimum
liability of one million dollars ($1,000,000.00) for the injury or death of any
one person and subject to the same limit per person, a minimum liability of one
million dollars ($1,000,000.00) for the injury or death of any number of
persons in one accident, and a minimum liability of one million dollars
($1,000,000.00) for damage to property of others, but excluding property of the
insured. The insurance certificate shall provide that notice shall be given to
the city clerk thirty (30) days prior to any cancellation or termination of
insurance. The cancellation or termination of the insurance shall automatically
revoke the permit.
E.   Additional Insured: The city shall be named as an additional insured under
all liability policies without expense to it. (1985 Code §3-4.0211; amd. 1993
Code)
4-5A-12: LICENSE FEE:
An annual license fee of one hundred dollars ($100.00) payable to the finance
director of the city shall accompany the initial application for license and
each application for renewal of the license. (1985 Code §3-4.0212; amd. 1993
Code; Ord. 1878, 8-23-2010, eff. 9-17-2010)
4-5A-13: RENEWAL REQUIREMENTS:
Applications for renewal need comply with the documentation requirements of
sections
4-5A-2 through
4-5A-11 of this article only in the event there has been a substantial change
in the conditions or circumstances on or off the site which significantly
affect the proposed operation or its effects during the proposed renewal
period, except that a showing must be made in such application that required
insurance is in force and has continued in force during the current license
year. The application for such renewal must specifically negate or affirm the
existence of any such circumstances or conditions and be documented
accordingly. The application for renewal must also be accompanied by a showing
of a current permit, issued by the appropriate state agency, for the operation
of the construction or demolition materials landfill site. The building
inspector, upon receipt of such application for renewal, shall process the same
as though it were an initial application for license, and shall report his
findings and recommendations thereon, which shall be reviewed by the council
before issuance of the renewal. (1985 Code §3-4.0213)
4-5A-14: SITE ACCESSIBILITY:
The location of the fence and gates, which shall be provided to exclude people
from the active fill site, shall be shown. They shall be located to prevent
illegal dumping, children from playing on the site, and debris from being blown
off the site. The fence shall be at least six feet (6') high and composed of a
metal fabric and it shall comply with all street intersection setback
requirements. The fence shall be constructed before landfill operations begin.
For purposes of this requirement, "active fill site" shall mean that portion of
the land covered by the license which is in fact regularly receiving waste
whether or not at the instance of the applicant. The applicant shall maintain
any unfenced area free of solid waste, and in the event of accumulation of
waste upon or abutting the site, the Building Inspector may require the
applicant to install such further fencing as can assure that the then-active
remainder of the site shall remain free of unauthorized or improper
accumulation of solid waste. (1985 Code §3-4.0214)
4-5A-15: SIGNING:
A prominent legible sign shall be provided at all site entrances indicating the
name of the site owner and operator and emergency telephone numbers. (1985 Code
§3-4.0215)
4-5A-16: PUBLIC AGENCIES:
Neither the City or any other public agency shall be required to obtain the
license required by this Article, but each such public body shall file with the
Council, before beginning operation and annually thereafter, evidence of
substantial compliance with all provisions of this Article except the
requirements of Section
4-5A-4 of this Article. It is, however, specifically provided that such
exemption from licensing shall not operate to exempt the City or other public
agencies from any other specific requirements of law relating to or regulating
such operation to which such operation would otherwise be subject. (1985 Code
§3-4.0216)
4-5A-17: PLAN CONTENT MANDATORY:
The operational details and physical site proposals contained in the plans
filed with an application which has been approved by the City Council shall be
obligatory and binding upon the licensee, who shall conform to each such detail
and proposal unless specifically relieved of such conformance by the Council.
(1985 Code §3-4.0217)
4-5A-18: REVOCATION OR DENIAL OF LICENSE RENEWAL:
In the event a licensee violates any section of this Article, as well as those
made obligatory and binding upon the licensee by reason of their inclusion in
the application and approval by the Council, or other City ordinances, then the
City Manager shall report the same to the Council, which shall set a public
hearing thereon and direct that the notice of the time, date and place of said
public hearing and of the City Manager's report be given to the licensee. Such
hearing shall occur not less than ten (10) days after such notice has been
mailed to the licensee at the address shown in the application or such other
address as has been provided by the licensee during the period of license. If,
upon said hearing, the Council determines noncompliance by the licensee, the
Council may revoke or suspend the license or, if such determination be made
while an application for renewal is pending, may deny renewal of the license.
Notice of such revocation or denial following such hearing may be either by
formal notice to the licensee at the appropriate address or by so advising
representatives of the licensee personally present at such hearing, or by any
other means reasonably calculated to apprise the licensee of such revocation or
such denial. No person or other legal entity whose license shall have been
revoked, or the renewal thereof denied, pursuant to this Section, and no
successors or assigns or other legal entities in which such person or other
legal entity shall have a substantial interest may obtain a license pursuant to
this Article within the City for a period of two (2) years from date of
cessation of activities at such landfill site pursuant to such revocation or
denial. The operation of a disposal site without having a presently valid
license to do so shall be and is hereby prohibited. (1985 Code §3-4.0218)
ARTICLE B. TRANSFER STATIONS
SECTION:
4-5B-1: Purpose
4-5B-2: License Required
4-5B-3: Application
4-5B-4: Insurance
4-5B-5: Licensing
4-5B-6: Disposal of Solid Waste
4-5B-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this Article is to regulate the location and operation of solid
waste transfer stations. (1985 Code §3-4.0301)
4-5B-2: LICENSE REQUIRED:
No person shall operate or permit the operation on its property, of a transfer
station in the City unless such person shall have first applied for and
received a license to do so from the City. A license to operate a transfer
station shall be issued by the Council upon application filed with the Building
Inspector of the City and accompanied by a special use permit issued by the
City Board of Adjustment, and a State permit issued by the appropriate State
agency, to conduct a transfer station operation on the site in question. The
applicant must show proof that he can demonstrate full present and contemplated
compliance with the specific provisions of this Article and the operational
details and physical site proposals contained in plans accompanying the
application, as well as the ability to do so; and shall be subject to annual
renewal by the Council as hereinafter set forth. In reviewing such application,
the Council must weigh the need for the transfer station against the potential
for site pollution, danger to persons or property likely to have direct or
indirect contact with the site, the feasibility of the operation, the
likelihood of freedom from negative environmental effect of such operation, and
such other factors as shall reflect the public interest in balance against the
interests of the applicant to operate such a facility on the site in question.
(1985 Code §3-4.0302)
4-5B-3: APPLICATION:
The application for a license to operate a transfer station shall be
accompanied by plans prepared under the direct supervision of a registered
engineer in conformity with chapter 114 of the Code of Iowa. The site as shown
on the plans shall physically conform to the following requirements, and the
application shall contain either sufficient written information to show such
conformity or it shall be shown by depiction of physical detail on the plan, as
applicable. (1985 Code §3-4.0303)
A.   Site: The site shall be located outside flood plain or riverfront land
unless such requirement is waived by the appropriate governmental agency or
agencies. The boundaries of the site shall be shown on the plan with sufficient
data, including legal description, that a land surveyor can easily locate the
boundaries. Two foot (2') contours of the existing terrain shall likewise be
shown on the plan. Proposed screening of the site from highways, streets,
parks, residences and other amenities, as well as the schedule of installation
of such, shall be shown; such screening shall meet the requirements of the
zoning ordinance and shall have been demonstrated to and approved by the City
Board of Adjustment. The site shall be enclosed with a chain link fence not
less than six feet (6') in height, which fence shall completely surround all
portions of the site intended to be used in connection with the operation of
the transfer station. The location of such fence shall be shown on the plan.
B.   Permits: The application will be accompanied by a copy of the special use
permit issued for such operation by the City Board of Adjustment and by a copy
of the permit issued by the applicable State agency, each approving the
operation of a transfer station on the site.
C.   Vehicular Travel: The plan shall show the areas on the site over which
haul vehicles and transfer equipment will travel. Such areas shall be
hardsurfaced, and the thickness and composition of such surfaces shall be shown
on the plans. Barricades of a semi-permanent nature, affixed to the ground,
shall be placed to prevent vehicular travel on unsurfaced areas on the site;
the location of such barricades shall be shown on the plan. The haul road
routes from the nearest City truck route shall be shown and identified on the
plan. Such routes shall be reviewed by the Engineering Department, who shall
make recommendations thereon to the Council. Such haul roads shall be chosen to
avoid undue hardship to residents living adjacent to them and to minimize the
likelihood of premature deterioration of City streets so chosen.
D.   Unloading Area: All unloading, compacting and transfer activities shall be
conducted within a fully enclosed structure or structures. Each such structure
shall be clearly depicted on the plan, with dimensions, in such fashion as to
clearly show the type and location of equipment, the proposed routing of
unloading and transfer vehicles, all vehicle entrance and exit facilities to
and from such structure or structures, and the waiting area for unloading
vehicles, which shall be sufficient to accommodate expected traffic. Such
structures and waiting area shall be of sufficient size and appropriate design
as will assure that the volume of vehicles expected on site at any one time can
be accommodated without spill-over on surrounding streets.
E.   Drainage and Sewers: Floor surfaces in each unloading, compacting and
transfer structure shall be so constructed that they can be cleaned by
flushing, and that they will permit the drainage of liquids without ponding;
all such floor surfaces shall be equipped with floor drains or sump pump and
with a trap or other mechanical device which shall prevent the passage of
solids, which system shall be connected to a sanitary sewer. A storm drainage
system for the site shall provide adequate storm drainage with minimum ponding
and shall connect to a storm sewer. All interior drainage lines from the
unloading, compacting and transfer areas as well as other drainage lines within
the site shall be adequate to handle the volumes of water and liquids which may
be expected. All drainage and sewerage systems, floor drains, floor surfaces
construction and locations of connections to sewers shall be clearly identified
in the plan, showing dimensions and composition where appropriate.
F.   Sanitation and Environmental Control: All solid waste shall be confined to
unloading, compacting and transfer structures, and all solid waste remaining at
the transfer station at the end of each day shall be stored in leakproof,
flyproof, and rodentproof containers. Vector control, principally rat abatement
and mosquito abatement, shall be the responsibility of the operator. The
transfer station site shall be kept in a suitable clean and sanitary condition
at all times. The application shall list the provisions at the site and the
schedule for cleaning vehicles, structures and grounds, as well as the intended
continuing vector control.
G.   Fire Prevention: Burning of solid waste, either open or controlled, is
prohibited at the transfer station site. If a fire hydrant is not located
adjacent to the property and within three hundred feet (300') of the unloading,
compacting and transfer structure or structures, then a fire hydrant shall be
so installed and connected to an appropriate extension of the water main. The
location of the nearest fire hydrants to the transfer station shall be shown on
the plan, as shall such installations and extensions, where applicable.
H.   Equipment: The transfer station shall be so designed and maintained that
the operational failure of one component part will not result in a total
shutdown of the operation. An inventory of the equipment to be used in
connection with the unloading, compacting and transfer operation shall be
contained in the application, as well as a list of backup equipment available
or, failing direct availability, the sources from which such equipment shall be
obtained in the event of need.
I.   Prohibited Materials: Sewage solids or liquids and hazardous wastes shall
not be unloaded or accepted at the transfer station. Solid waste material of
such bulk as cannot be accommodated by direct transfer shall likewise be
excluded from the transfer station.
J.   Recycling: If the operation of the transfer station includes isolation,
segregation and gathering of materials of a like or similar kind for salvage
and reutilization by recycling, the equipment, methods, and proposed operation
in connection therewith shall be fully depicted and described in the
application. Solid waste which is received at the transfer station site and
which is not thereat separated for recycling may only be disposed of by hauling
to a sanitary disposal project which has been approved by the appropriate
governmental agency or agencies and is legally operating. Scavenging at the
transfer station site shall be prohibited, and all materials so separated and
gathered for salvage and reutilization by recycling shall be retained in
suitable containers as heretofore described until removed by appropriate
vehicles to off-site destinations,
K.   Personnel and Hours: The personnel planned to operate the site, the times
during which the gates will be open, and the hours and days of the week during
which the site will be open to receive solid waste shall be indicated in the
application. Appropriate signs meeting the requirements of the Zoning Ordinance
for the district in which located shall be located at all entrance gates, shall
be lighted if appropriate, shall identify such hours, shall list prohibited
materials, and shall contain such further information as will assure
conformance of visitors to the site to the requirements of this Article. An
attendant shall be on duty at the site at all times when it is open for public
use. (1985 Code §3-4.0303)
4-5B-4: INSURANCE:
The applicant shall file a certificate of insurance evidencing the issuance to
the applicant of liability insurance which shall protect the public and any and
all persons from injury which may be sustained by reason of the operation or
condition of the transfer station, and that the applicant carries insurance
which meets the requirements of the Iowa workmen's compensation law. Proof of
such insurance shall show a minimum cancellation time of ten (10) days and
shall embody a requirement that the City shall have a right to such notice
before such cancellation can become effective. The proof shall specify evidence
of the following forms of insurance protection:
A.   Operations Liability: Liability insurance covering all operations
performed by the licensed applicant and all persons in the licensed applicant's
direct employment.
B.   Subcontractor Liability: Public liability insurance covering all
operations performed by any subcontractor or independent contractor to whom a
portion of the operations may have been assigned or which in the future may be
assigned, or by any person or legal entity acting for or on behalf of the
licensed applicant at or on the site.
C.   Vehicle: Motor vehicle bodily injury insurance and property damage
liability insurance on motor vehicles employed on the site, whether or not
owned by the licensed applicant or by either the subcontractors or independent
contractors under contract to the licensee, or by any other person or legal
entity acting for or on behalf of the licensed applicant at or on the site.
D.   Amounts: The main protection shall be insurance coverage with a minimum
liability of one million dollars ($1,000,000.00) for the injury or death of any
one person and subject to the same limit per person, a minimum liability of one
million dollars ($1,000,000.00) for the injury or death of any number of
persons in one accident, and a minimum liability of one million dollars
($1,000,000.00) for damage to property of others, but excluding property of the
insured. The insurance certificate shall provide that notice shall be given to
the city clerk thirty (30) days prior to any cancellation or termination of
insurance. The cancellation or termination of the insurance shall automatically
revoke the permit.
E.   Additional Insured: The city shall be named as an additional insured under
all liability policies without expense to it. (1985 Code §3-4.0304; amd. 1993
Code)
4-5B-5: LICENSING:
A.   License Fee; Renewal: An annual license fee of one hundred dollars
($100.00) payable to the finance director shall accompany the initial
application for license and each application for renewal of the license. The
provisions of article A of this chapter for renewal of license for construction
or demolition materials disposal sites shall likewise apply to the annual
renewal of a transfer station license. (1985 Code §3-4.0305; amd. 1993 Code;
Ord. 1878, 8-23-2010, eff. 9-17-2010)
B.   Public Agencies: Neither the city nor any other public agency shall be
required to obtain the license required by this article, but each such public
body shall file with the council, before beginning operation and annually
thereafter, evidence of substantial compliance with all provisions of this
article except the requirements of sections
4-5B-2 and
4-5B-4 of this article and subsections A and C of this section. It is, however,
specifically provided that such exemption from licensing shall not operate to
exempt the city or other public agencies from any other specific requirements
of law relating to or regulating such operation to which such operation would
be otherwise subject. (1985 Code §3-4.0307)
C.   Revocation Or Denial: The provisions of article A of this chapter for
revocation or denial of renewal of a license for construction or demolition
materials disposal sites shall apply to the license of a transfer station.
(1985 Code §3-4.0307)
4-5B-6: DISPOSAL OF SOLID WASTE:
All persons operating a transfer station licensed under the provisions of this
article shall deliver or cause to be delivered all solid waste coming within
its control to the Des Moines metropolitan area solid waste agency disposal
site or sites. (1985 Code §3-4.0308)
ARTICLE C. FEES AND CHARGES
SECTION:
4-5C-1: Fees Established
4-5C-2: When Fees Imposed
4-5C-3: Monthly Charges
4-5C-4: Proration Of Charges
4-5C-5: Exemption From Fees; Special Conditions
4-5C-6: Periodic Review Of Charges; Annual Report
4-5C-7: Administrative Fees; Transmittal Of Receipts
4-5C-8: Lien For Nonpayment
4-5C-1: FEES ESTABLISHED:
The member municipality will fix, establish and maintain and revise the same
from time to time whenever necessary such rates, fees, rentals or other charges
for the use and services of the disposal facilities operated by the agency, as
more fully described in the solid waste disposal service contract, as will
always provide in each year revenues sufficient to pay the proportionate share
of such member municipality for: a) operation and maintenance expenses for said
disposal facilities; b) collection, recycling, billing and spring cleanup fees;
c) administrative fees; d) the principal and interest on the solid waste
disposal revenue bonds; and e) all reserves, renewal and replacement funds and
other funds provided for in the resolution authorizing the issuance of such
solid waste disposal revenue bonds. (Ord. 1425, 10-30-2000, eff. 12-4-2000)
4-5C-2: WHEN FEES IMPOSED:
An initial schedule of such rates, fees, tolls and other charges to be levied
and collected from the residents of the member municipality for the use and
services of said disposal facilities shall be established and put into effect
whenever necessary in order for said member municipality to comply with the
provisions of its solid waste disposal service contract; provided, however, the
member municipality may in its discretion apply such other lawfully available
monies it has on hand for such purpose. (1985 Code §3-4.0403)
4-5C-3: MONTHLY CHARGES:
There is herewith imposed a solid waste collection and disposal fee as follows
applicable to each residential unit for solid waste collected by the city
approved contractor:
 
48 gallon cart - $16.00 per month
96 gallon cart - 16.66 per month
 
Charges for collection of additional carts shall be as follows:
 
48 gallon cart - $8.50 per month
96 gallon cart - 9.05 per month
 
These charges shall be made on all bills mailed by West Des Moines Water Works
on and after the effective date hereof. Additional charges may also be imposed
for changing cart size. The collection agent for the city shall be the West Des
Moines Water Works which shall provide for solid waste charges to be listed
upon its regular billing statement and collected in the same manner as water
and sanitary sewer fees. Billing for the change in container size shall be made
in the billing cycle following the change. All charges imposed herein shall be
due and payable upon receipt of the billing. (Ord. 2373, 7-1-2019; amd. Ord.
2481, 7-6-2021; Ord. 2574, 7-17-2023; Ord. 2611, 5-20-2024; Ord. 2657, 4-7-
2025)
4-5C-4: PRORATION OF CHARGES:
The service availability charge shall be prorated according to the ratio of the
number of days for which solid waste collection service was available to a
customer at a premises and the total number of days in the month. (Ord. 2373,
7-1-2019; Ord. 2574, 7-17-2023)
4-5C-5: EXEMPTION FROM FEES; SPECIAL CONDITIONS:
In special conditions including, but not limited to, the instances noted below,
the City Manager may, upon a written request for an exemption of fees filed
with West Des Moines Water Works, grant fee payment and collection variances
after determining that granting the variance would be in the City's best
interest, will improve efficiency, safety and is practical. Upon the granting
of any variance, the City Manager shall file notice with the City Council
giving reason(s) for the variance.
A.   If an individual receives water service from West Des Moines Water Works
and, for whatever reason which results in the building being vacant or
unoccupied, desires and pays West Des Moines Water Works for shutting off said
service for a period of not less than two (2) weeks.
B.   If a building serves a mixed use (i.e., residential and commercial), the
City will classify the entire building commercial with the property owner then
required to contract with a private solid waste hauler who shall guarantee
collection on a frequency at least equal to collections by the City.
C.   Unoccupied unit(s) within a building which is either uninhabitable and/or
if no certificate of occupancy or rental has been granted by the City;
provided, that the unit(s) is vacant for a period of not less than two (2)
weeks.
D.   Housing units of a condominium or townhouse nature, where private drives,
streets or common areas exist making it impractical for all residents of a
development to place solid waste at the public street curb, and where the City,
pursuant to other sections of this article, would normally be responsible for
collection and disposal of waste may contract for private solid waste service;
provided, that the private solid waste hauler guarantees collection from all
housing units within that development on a frequency at least equal to
collections by the City. (Ord. 966, 8-19-1991)
E.   The City Manager, in his sole discretion, may authorize solid waste
service charge credits in unique situations, on a case by case basis. (Ord.
1525, 4-28-2003, eff. 7-1-2003)
4-5C-6: PERIODIC REVIEW OF CHARGES; ANNUAL REPORT:
On an annual basis the City Manager shall submit to the City Council a report
summarizing all solid waste activities occurring during the previous period,
and listing all revenues and costs associated therewith. The City Council shall
then review said report with respect to service charges imposed herein, and
goals and objectives to be accomplished as part of the general City operations.
(1985 Code §3-4.0407)
4-5C-7: ADMINISTRATIVE FEES; TRANSMITTAL OF RECEIPTS:
The West Des Moines Water Works may, before transmitting to the City Finance
Director receipts from solid waste collections, subtract an administrative and
accounting fee not to exceed thirty cents ($0.30) per customer billing
applicable to charges for solid waste collection. All funds received pursuant
to this article, minus administrative charges shall be paid by the Water Works
to the Finance Director not later than seventy five (75) days following the
applicable billing due date. (1985 Code §3-4.0408; amd. 1993 Code; Ord. 1425,
10-30-2000, eff. 12-4-2000; Ord. 1878, 8-23-2010, eff. 9-17-2010)
4-5C-8: LIEN FOR NONPAYMENT:
Each delinquent account which is transmitted to the Finance Department by the
West Des Moines Water Works shall thereafter be processed for imposition of a
lien upon the contributor's property as provided by section 384.84 of the Iowa
Code, in the amount of the delinquent account, plus a County administrative fee
for each lien certified as provided in section 384.84 of the Iowa Code, plus a
City delinquency fee in the amount of ten dollars ($10.00) to recoup the City's
administrative processing costs and lost investment on the unpaid amount. The
lien here provided shall apply only to that property or those properties for
which the contributor's account is delinquent. (Ord. 1084, 3-28-1994, eff. 7-1-
1994; amd. Ord. 1425, 10-30-2000, eff. 12-4-2000; Ord. 1878, 8-23-2010, eff. 9-
17-2010)
CHAPTER 6
MUNICIPAL RECYCLING
SECTION:
4-6-1: Purpose
4-6-2: Definitions
4-6-3: Establishment Of Recycling Program
4-6-4: Reporting Requirements
4-6-5: Authorization Of Collectors
4-6-6: License Application, Term, Revocation (Rep. by Ord. 2324, 8-6-2018)
4-6-7: Applicability Of Regulations
4-6-8: Collection And Transportation Of Designated Recyclable Materials
4-6-9: Storage Of Designated Recyclable Materials
4-6-10: Preparation Of Designated Recyclable Materials And Placement For
Collection
4-6-11: Collection By Unauthorized Persons
4-6-12: Enforcement
4-6-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this chapter is to promote recycling by requiring property
owners to provide facilities for the source separation of recyclable materials
at certain locations. (Ord. 1128, 4-24-1995)
4-6-2: DEFINITIONS:
The following words and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have, unless
the context clearly indicates otherwise, the meanings given to them in this
section:
CITY: The City of West Des Moines.
COLLECTION: The transportation of the Municipal waste from the place it is
generated and includes all activities up to the time the waste is delivered to
a recycling facility or solid waste disposal site.
COLLECTOR: A person authorized by the City to collect, transport and dispose of
Municipal waste or recyclable materials.
COMMINGLED: Source separated, nonputrescible recyclable materials that have
been mixed at the source of generation (i.e., placed in the same container).
CONDOMINIUM: An apartment building or housing area in which the dwelling units
are owned individually.
DESIGNATED RECYCLABLE MATERIAL: Newspapers, corrugated containers, magazines,
catalogs, junk mail, kraft bags, bi- metal and ferrous cans, aluminum cans,
clear glass containers, high density polyethylene (HDPE) (excluding motor oil
bottles), and polyethylene terephthalate (PETE), whether alone or in
combination.
DWELLING UNIT: A group of rooms located within a structure and forming a single
habitable unit with facilities which are used or intended to be used for
living, sleeping, cooking and eating for the exclusive use of the occupants
thereof.
MULTI-FAMILY DWELLING: Any building under one roof which contains two (2) or
more complete dwelling units, or a detached townhome that is located in a
multi-family zoning district.
MUNICIPAL WASTE: Any garbage, refuse, industrial lunchroom or office waste, and
other material, including solid, liquid, semi-solid or contained gaseous
material resulting from the operation of multi-family dwellings.
NEARBY: Adjoining, adjacent, or contiguous.
NONRECYCLABLE MATERIAL: Any material not defined as recyclable material.
PERSON: Any individual, partnership, corporation, association, institution,
cooperative enterprises, or any other legal entity whatsoever which is
recognized by law as being subject to such rights and duties.
PREMISES: Real property on which any multi-family dwelling unit or combination
of units sharing common driveways are located.
RECYCLING: The separation, collection, processing, recovering and sale or reuse
of materials which would otherwise be disposed of as Municipal waste.
RECYCLING FACILITY: Any facility employing a technology that is a process that
separates or recovers reusable materials that can be sold or reused by a
manufacturer as substitute for or a supplement to virgin raw materials.
SOURCE SEPARATION: The separation of recyclable materials from the Municipal
waste stream at the point of waste generation. (Ord. 1128, 4-24-1995; amd. Ord.
2669, 9-15-2025)
4-6-3: ESTABLISHMENT OF RECYCLING PROGRAM:
A.   There is hereby established a recycling program for the source separation,
separate collection and recycling of designated recyclable materials generated
within the City from all multi-family dwellings and dwelling units not
presently served by existing residential recycling collection programs.
B.   Collection of designated recyclable materials pursuant to this section
shall be made at least twice per month, or more often as necessary, as
determined by the Director of Public Works or other designee of the City
Manager, and the storage of said designated recyclable materials shall not
result in the creation of a public nuisance.
C.   All multi-family dwellings which are not presently part of existing
residential recycling collection programs shall be required to provide the
facilities for the source separation of all designated recyclable materials
generated on the premises and shall arrange for the collection of said
materials to be transported to a recycling facility.
D.   Program development, implementation and operation shall be the
responsibility of the same entity which contracts for the private collection
and disposal of solid waste on the premises.
E.   The specific "designated recyclable materials" are those materials set out
in section
4-6-2 of this chapter.
F.   The City reserves the right to amend the list of "designated recyclable
materials" as defined in section
4-6-2 of this chapter at any time. (Ord. 1128, 4-24-1995)
4-6-4: REPORTING REQUIREMENTS:
It shall be the responsibility of all commercial waste haulers collecting solid
waste or designated recyclable materials generated in the City to submit a
recycling report to the City on an annual basis. Said report shall identify
individual establishments being served and the total weight of recyclable
materials collected as well as identification of the processor of each
recovered recyclable material. All such reports of the previous year shall be
submitted, on forms provided by the City, to the Director of Public Works or
other designee of the City Manager by January 31. The City reserves the right
to require any additional information deemed necessary by the Director of
Public Works or other designee of the City Manager. (Ord. 1128, 4-24-1995)
4-6-5: AUTHORIZATION OF COLLECTORS:
All commercial solid waste haulers or haulers of designated recyclable
materials who as a commercial enterprise provide the service of collection of
said designated recyclable materials or waste to owners/operators of multi-
family dwelling units shall be duly authorized by the Department of Public
Works through the issuance of a license. (Ord. 1128, 4-24-1995)
4-6-6: LICENSE APPLICATION, TERM, REVOCATION:
(Rep. by Ord. 2324, 8-6-2018)
4-6-7: APPLICABILITY OF REGULATIONS:
Any person or persons engaged in the collection, processing and marketing of
designated recyclable materials within the City or who collects solid waste
within the City, and all householders, firms, corporations, co-partnerships and
any and all persons who may or do produce solid waste and/or designated
recyclable materials shall be subject to the provisions of this chapter. (Ord.
1128, 4-24-1995)
4-6-8: COLLECTION AND TRANSPORTATION OF DESIGNATED RECYCLABLE MATERIALS:
A.   Transportation: Any person transporting designated recyclable materials
within the City shall prevent or remedy any spillage from vehicles or
containers used in the transport of such designated recyclable materials. Such
vehicles or containers shall not be overfilled and shall be cleansed at
sufficiently frequent intervals to prevent obnoxious odors or unhealthful
conditions. Such vehicles shall also be so constructed, loaded and driven so as
to prevent any portion of the load from falling out upon the streets or
highways.
B.   Removal By Collectors: Collectors shall return the recycling receptacles
to the premises from which they have been removed in a manner so as not to
create a public nuisance. Collectors shall also collect and remove all
recyclable materials for which they are responsible to collect from the
premises. (Ord. 1128, 4-24-1995)
4-6-9: STORAGE OF DESIGNATED RECYCLABLE MATERIALS:
A.   General: It shall be the duty of every owner or entity which contracts for
the private collection and disposal of solid waste from the premises to provide
and keep at all times, a sufficient number of containers to hold all designated
recyclable materials which may accumulate during the intervals between
collection of such materials by the authorized collector. Containers may be
located on-site or on nearby premises with the permission of the affected
property owner or otherwise in accordance with the provision of this section.
Owners of multi-family dwelling units shall insure that each dwelling unit has
access to the containers and that said containers are sufficient to hold all
designated recyclable materials accumulated by the occupants of the dwelling
unit during the intervals between collections.
B.   Storage: All designated recyclable materials accumulated by owners and/or
occupants of multi-family dwelling units shall be placed in containers which
are durable, watertight and made of metal or plastic and marked with the
recycling symbol or other acceptable markings. The containers shall remain on
the premises at all times and shall be kept in a clean condition. The type of
bulk container to be furnished by the collector shall be acceptable to the
Director of Public Works or other designee of the City Manager. Containers
shall have lids if necessary to avert a public nuisance or protect the
marketing quality of designated recyclable materials. Such lids must remain
closed except when designated recyclable materials are being placed in or
removed from the container. The container shall be clearly marked with both the
recycling symbol and with the type of material(s) to be deposited in the
container. The container shall be kept clean and in good repair. The number of
such containers shall be sufficient to handle the volume of recyclables which
accumulate between collection intervals.
C.   Location Of Containers: Bulk storage containers for collection at multi-
family dwellings using private collection shall be located on such premises at
a place agreed upon by such owner or occupant of the property and the
authorized collector. Such location shall not interfere with private or public
sidewalks, walkways, driveways, roads, streets, highways or entrances and exits
of private or public buildings and shall be in compliance with all applicable
laws. Bulk storage containers which are on wheels to facilitate their movement
shall remain blocked at all times while unattended to prevent unintentional
movement. (Ord. 1128, 4-24-1995)
4-6-10: PREPARATION OF DESIGNATED RECYCLABLE MATERIALS AND PLACEMENT FOR
COLLECTION:
Designated recyclable materials shall be separated and prepared in a manner
consistent with recycling market requirements and placed at a designated area
separate from Municipal waste for collection at such time and dates as may be
agreed upon between the collector and the establishment. (Ord. 1128, 4-24-1995)
A.   No person shall place, drop, commingle or deposit in recyclable material
any solid waste or banned substance, as defined in section
4-5-3 of this title, into any designated recyclable material container, bin or
dumpster located on any premises.
Any person who violates the provisions of this subsection shall, upon
conviction, be subject to a fine of not to exceed one hundred dollars ($100.00)
or imprisonment not to exceed thirty (30) days. (Ord. 1158, 11-8-1995)
4-6-11: COLLECTION BY UNAUTHORIZED PERSONS:
A.   It shall be a violation of this chapter for any person(s) unauthorized by
the City to collect or pick up, or cause to be collected or picked up, any
recyclable materials or solid waste. Each such collection in violation hereof
shall constitute a separate and distinct offense and shall be subject to the
following civil penalties:
1.   One hundred dollars ($100.00) for the first offense;
2.   Five hundred dollars ($500.00) for the second offense; and
3.   One thousand dollars ($1,000.00) for each subsequent offense.
B.   Notwithstanding any provision of this chapter, any person having ownership
of the same may sell or donate recyclable materials for the purpose of
recycling to any person, partnership or corporation, whether operating for
profit or not for profit. (Ord. 1128, 4-24-1995)
4-6-12: ENFORCEMENT:
A.   Administration: The City's Department of Community Development is hereby
authorized and directed to administer and enforce this chapter. At apartment
complexes, Community Development Department personnel will tie recycling
compliance into their biannual multi-family inspections and include it on the
inspector's checklist. Enforcement relative to multi- family recycling may also
be handled by more frequent inspections or on a complaint basis. (Ord. 1128, 4-
24-1995)
B.   Violation And Penalty: Except as set forth in subsection
4-6-10A of this chapter, any person who shall fail, neglect or refuse to comply
with any terms or provisions of this chapter or any regulation or requirement
pursuant thereto and authorized thereby, shall be subject to a civil penalty of
one dollar ($1.00) per month for each dwelling unit on the premises in
violation of this chapter. (Ord. 1158, 11-8-1995)
CHAPTER 7
NOISE CONTROL
SECTION:
4-7-1: Title
4-7-2: Policy
4-7-3: Purpose
4-7-4: Definitions
4-7-5: Measurement Of Noise And Sound
4-7-6: Test Measurement And Requirements For Determination And Classification
Of Sound
4-7-7: Maximum Permissible Sound Levels By Receiving Land Use
4-7-8: Exceptions To This Chapter
4-7-9: Vehicle Noise Limits
4-7-10: General Prohibition
4-7-11: Regulation Of Sound Equipment And Sound Amplifying Equipment
4-7-12: Conditions Of Sound Permit Approval
4-7-13: Prior Determination For Sound Permit Approval
4-7-14: Appeals
4-7-15: Enforcement
4-7-16: Penalties
4-7-1: TITLE:
A.   These regulations shall be officially known, cited, and referred to as the
NOISE CONTROL REGULATIONS OF THE CITY OF WEST DES MOINES, IOWA (hereinafter
"these regulations"). (Ord. 1892, 11-29-2010)
4-7-2: POLICY:
A.   Excessive noise is a serious hazard to the public health and welfare and
the quality of life in a close urban society.
B.   A substantial body of science and technology exists by which excessive
noise can be substantially abated without serious inconvenience to the public.
C.   Certain noise producing equipment in this community is essential to the
quality of life herein and should be allowed to continue at reasonable levels
with moderate regulation.
D.   Each person has the right to an environment reasonably free from noise
which jeopardizes health, welfare, or which unduly interferes with a property
owner's right to the use or enjoyment of their property.
E.   It is recognized that residential land uses are more noise sensitive than
commercial and industrial land uses, and that commercial land uses are more
noise sensitive than industrial land uses.
F.   It is the declared policy of this city to promote an environment free from
excessive noise, otherwise properly called "noise pollution", which
unreasonably jeopardizes the health and welfare and degrades the quality of the
lives of the residents of this community, without unduly prohibiting, limiting,
or otherwise regulating the function of certain noise producing equipment and
events which is not amenable to such controls and yet is essential to the
economy and quality of life of the community. (Ord. 1892, 11-29-2010)
4-7-3: PURPOSE:
A.   These regulations are adopted for the following purposes:
1.   To address concerns expressed by citizens and businesses of this
community.
2.   To establish standards for the control of noise pollution in the city by
setting maximum permissible sound levels for various land uses.
3.   To protect and provide for the public health, safety, and general welfare
of the city.
4.   This chapter shall apply to the control of noise originating within the
limits of the city. (Ord. 1892, 11-29-2010)
4-7-4: DEFINITIONS:
A.   For the purpose of this chapter, certain terms or words used herein shall
be interpreted as follows:
A-WEIGHTED SOUND LEVEL: The sound pressure level in decibels as measured on a
sound level meter using the A-weighted filter network.
ADVERSE IMPACT: A state of facts as would lead a reasonable person of normal
sensitivity acting prudently to conclude that the economic, entertainment, and
philanthropic benefits to the community do not reasonably outweigh the quiet
use and enjoyment of the affected property.
AMBIENT LEVEL: All encompassing sound at a given place, usually a composite of
sounds from many sources near and far.
AMPLIFIED SOUND: The production or reproduction of sound from amplification
equipment.
BACKGROUND LEVEL: Ambient level sound less the noise disturbance.
C-WEIGHTED SOUND LEVEL: The sound pressure level in decibels as measured on a
sound level meter using the C-weighted filter network.
CONSTRUCTION: Any site preparation, assembly, erection, substantial repair,
alteration, or similar action, for or of public or private rights of way,
structures, utilities, or similar property.
dBA: Decibels measured using an A-weighted sound level.
dBC: Decibels measured using a C-weighted sound level.
DECIBEL (dB): A unit for measuring the amplitude of a sound, equal to twenty
(20) times the logarithm to the base 10 of the ratio of the pressure of the
sound measured to the reference pressure, which is twenty (20) micropascals.
DEMOLITION: Any dismantling, intentional destruction or removal of structures,
utilities, public or private right of way surfaces, or similar property.
EMERGENCY: Any occurrence or set of circumstances involving actual or imminent
physical or psychological trauma or property damage which demands immediate
action.
EMERGENCY WORK: Any work performed for the purpose of alleviating or resolving
an emergency.
L5A: The A-weighted sound level exceeded five percent (5%) of the ten (10)
minute sound meter reading, or more than thirty (30) seconds in total.
L5C: The C-weighted sound level exceeded five percent (5%) of the ten (10)
minute sound meter reading, or more than thirty (30) seconds in total.
NOISE: Any sound which disturbs humans or which causes or tends to cause an
adverse psychological or physiological effect on humans.
NOISE DISTURBANCE: Any sound which endangers or injures the welfare, safety, or
health of a human being, or disturbs a reasonable person of normal
sensitivities, or devalues or injures personal or real property.
NOISE SENSITIVE LAND USE: Those specific land uses which have associated indoor
and/or outdoor human activities that may be subject to stress and/or
significant interference from noise produced by community sound sources. Such
human activity typically occurs daily for continuous periods of twenty four
(24) hours or is in such a nature that noise is significantly disruptive to
activities that occur for short periods. Specifically, noise sensitive land
uses include: hospitals, rest homes, convalescent care facilities, places of
worship, and schools.
PERSON: A natural person, heirs, executors, administrators or assigns, and also
includes a firm, partnership, or corporation, its or their successors or
assigns, or the agent of any of the aforesaid.
PLAINLY AUDIBLE: Any noise or sound for which the information content of the
noise or sound is transferred to the listener such as, but not limited to,
understanding of spoken speech, comprehension of whether a voice is raised or
lowered, or comprehension of musical rhythms.
PUBLIC RIGHT OF WAY: Any street, avenue, boulevard, highway, sidewalk, alley,
or similar place which is owned or controlled by a governmental entity.
PUBLIC SPACE: Any real property, including any structure thereon, which is
owned or controlled by a governmental entity.
RECEIVING LAND USE: The use or occupancy of the property which receives the
transmission of "sound" as hereinafter defined.
SOUND: An oscillation in pressure, particle displacement, particle velocity, or
other physical parameter, in a medium with internal forces that cause
compression and rarefaction of that medium. The description of sound may
include any characteristic of such sound, including duration, intensity, and
frequency.
SOUND AMPLIFYING EQUIPMENT: Any machine or device for the amplification of the
human voice, music, or any other sound.
SOUND EQUIPMENT: Any radio, record player, stereo, television, compact disc
player, tape deck or player, loudspeakers, amplifier, sound truck, or other
device for producing, reproducing, or amplifying sounds.
SOUND LEVEL (NOISE LEVEL): The weighted sound pressure level obtained by use of
a sound level meter having a standard frequency filter for attenuating part of
the sound spectrum.
SOUND LEVEL METER: An instrument, including a microphone, an amplifier, an
output meter, and frequency weighting networks for the measurement and
determination of noise and sound levels. (Ord. 1892, 11-29-2010)
4-7-5: MEASUREMENT OF NOISE AND SOUND:
The measurement of noise or sound shall be made with a sound level meter
meeting the standards prescribed by the American National Standards Institute.
(Ord. 1892, 11-29-2010)
4-7-6: TEST MEASUREMENT AND REQUIREMENTS FOR DETERMINATION AND CLASSIFICATION
OF SOUND:
A.   For the purposes of determining and classifying any sound as excessive or
unusually loud, the following test measurement and requirements are to be
applied:
1.   The sound must be measured at or within the property boundary of the
receiving land use.
2.   Unamplified sound shall be measured on a sound level meter of standard
design and quality operated in "A" slow response weighing scale.
3.   Amplified sound shall be measured on a sound level meter of standard
design and quality operated in "C" slow response weighing scale.
4.   A sound measured or registered in excess of the maximum permitted levels
is prohibited.
5.   A ten (10) minute L5A or L5C ambient level measurement must be taken to
determine whether the sound disturbance exceeds the maximum permissible level
allowed for a receiving land use. A one minute L5A or L5C background level
measurement should also be taken when the sound disturbance is inactive. The
ambient level measurement must be a minimum of ten (10) dB above the background
level measurement to attribute the noise to the sound disturbance. The one
minute L5A or L5C background level measurement shall be deemed to be the
background level measurement that existed at the time of the ambient level
measurement. The person responsible for the sound disturbance must render the
noise inactive for the purposes of a one minute background level measurement
within thirty (30) minutes of a request to do so by a police officer or other
city official authorized to enforce the provisions of this chapter. If the
person responsible fails to timely render the noise inactive for the one minute
background level measurement, that person thereby waives the ten (10) dB
difference requirement and the result of the ten (10) minute ambient level
measurement shall be deemed to be the noise attributed to the sound
disturbance. (Ord. 1892, 11-29-2010)
4-7-7: MAXIMUM PERMISSIBLE SOUND LEVELS BY RECEIVING LAND USE:
A.   With the exception of sound levels elsewhere specifically authorized or
allowed in this chapter, the following are maximum permissible sound levels
allowed at or within the property boundary of a receiving land use for
unamplified sound:
 
Receiving Land Use Maximum L5A Level Permitted
                   7 A.M. - 7 P.M. 7 P.M. - 10 P.M. 10 P.M. - 7 A.M.
Residential        65 dBA          60 dBA           55 dBA
Commercial         65 dBA          65 dBA           65 dBA
Industrial         80 dBA          80 dBA           80 dBA
Noise sensitive    65 dBA          60 dBA           55 dBA
 
B.   With the exception of sound levels elsewhere specifically authorized or
allowed in this chapter, the following are maximum permissible sound levels
allowed at or within the property boundary of a receiving land use for
amplified sound:
 
Receiving Land Use Maximum L5C Level Permitted
                   7 A.M. - 7 P.M. 7 P.M. - 10 P.M. 10 P.M. - 7 A.M.
Residential        76 dBC          74 dBC           72 dBC
Commercial         82 dBC          80 dBC           78 dBC
Industrial         85 dBC          85 dBC           85 dBC
Noise sensitive    76 dBC          74 dBC           72 dBC
 
C.   If the volume of sound exceeds the maximum permissible sound level by a
measurement of L5A or L5C, at any time during a ten (10) minute meter reading,
the sound is prohibited and is in violation of this chapter. (Ord. 1892, 11-29-
2010)
4-7-8: EXCEPTIONS TO THIS CHAPTER:
A.   The maximum permissible sound levels of this chapter shall not apply to:
1.   The emission of sound made by safety signals, warning devices, and sound
resulting from any authorized emergency vehicle when responding to an emergency
call or acting in time of an emergency. An authorized emergency vehicle shall
include local, state, and federal law enforcement vehicles, emergency medical
vehicles, and fire department vehicles.
2.   Noncommercial public speaking and public assembly activities conducted on
any public space, or public right of way, during the hours of seven o'clock (7:
00) A.M. to ten o'clock (10:00) P.M.
3.   The emission of sound through the unamplified human voice.
4.   Agricultural activities associated with the raising and harvesting of
crops, exclusive of those involving the ownership or possession of animals or
birds.
5.   Rail and air transportation and public mass transportation vehicles.
6.   The emission of sound in the performance of military operations, exclusive
of travel by individuals to or from military duty.
7.   The emission of sound from activities in the discharge of weapons,
fireworks, displays, parades, concerts, or other events expressly permitted or
authorized by the city council. This exception includes outdoor Historic Valley
Junction Foundation events as long as such events conclude by eight thirty
o'clock (8:30) P.M. The outdoor Historic Valley Junction Foundation events may
be permitted to extend past eight thirty o'clock (8:30) P.M., but are subject
to city approval and the maximum permissible sound levels prescribed within
this chapter.
8.   The emission of sound from activities where a state or federal agency has
adopted a different standard or rules than that prescribed within this chapter.
9.   The emission of sound during nonprofessional athletic and school events or
practices.
10.   The emission of sound during demolition work, construction work for which
a building permit, grading permit, or demolition permit is required, or a
development plan approved. In cases where the sound originates within three
hundred feet (300') of a residential land use or noise sensitive land use, the
exemption shall only apply between the hours of seven o'clock (7:00) A.M. to
ten o'clock (10:00) P.M.
11.   The emission of sound from the use of lawn and garden equipment and chain
saws. In cases where the sound originates within three hundred feet (300') of a
residential land use or noise sensitive land use, the exemption shall only
apply between the hours of seven o'clock (7:00) A.M. to ten o'clock (10:00)
P.M.
12.   The emission of sound from the use of snow removal equipment.
13.   The emission of sound from on site stationary trash compactors. In cases
where the sound originates within three hundred feet (300') of a residential
land use or noise sensitive land use, the exemption shall only apply between
the hours of seven o'clock (7:00) A.M. to ten o'clock (10:00) P.M.
14.   The emission of sound from municipal or municipally contracted compactor
trucks loading or unloading of yard waste, recyclable material, trash, and
garbage.
15.   The operation of private compactor trucks in the loading and unloading of
yard waste, recyclable material, trash, and garbage on private property. In
cases where the sound originates within three hundred feet (300') of a
residential land use or noise sensitive land use, the exemption shall only
apply between the hours of seven o'clock (7:00) A.M. to ten o'clock (10:00)
P.M.
16.   The emission of sound during the operation, maintenance, repair, and
cleaning of public streets and facilities.
17.   The emission of sound during public and private parking lot maintenance
and repair. In cases where the sound originates within three hundred feet
(300') of a residential land use or noise sensitive land use, the exemption
shall only apply between the hours of seven o'clock (7:00) A.M. to ten o'clock
(10:00) P.M.
18.   Work performed by or for public utilities.
19.   Live radio broadcasts as long as such broadcasts utilize fifty (50) watts
or less of electrical power as provided in subsection
 4-7-11J of this chapter.
B.   Although exempt from the maximum permissible sound levels of this chapter,
a sound equipment permit is required in all cases where sound equipment and
sound amplifying equipment will be used unless explicitly exempted within this
chapter. (Ord. 2053, 9-8-2014, eff. 1-1-2015)
4-7-9: VEHICLE NOISE LIMITS:
No person shall operate or control a motor vehicle, which is moving or
stationary, standing or parked, whether or not persons are seated in the motor
vehicle, from which any amplified sound is plainly audible at a distance of
fifty feet (50') from the vehicle between the hours of seven o'clock (7:00)
A.M. and ten o'clock (10:00) P.M., or is plainly audible at a distance of
twenty five feet (25') from the vehicle between the hours of ten o'clock (10:
00) P.M. and seven o'clock (7:00) A.M. (Ord. 1892, 11-29-2010)
4-7-10: GENERAL PROHIBITION:
A.   No person shall engage or participate in activities which result in noise
levels which exceed the maximum permitted noise levels outlined in section
4-7-7 of this chapter.
B.   It shall be the duty of the owner to prevent such premises or vehicles
from being the site of such activities producing sound levels in excess of what
is permitted under this chapter. Failure or refusal to perform such duty shall
constitute a violation of this section. The owner may include one or more of
the following: fee title owner, lessee, and other persons granted a legal right
to exercise use of the property.
C.   It shall be the duty of persons in positions of leadership or
responsibility with respect to unincorporated associations, groups, gatherings,
or assemblages of people to prevent such from causing or making sound levels in
excess of what is permitted under this chapter. (Ord. 1892, 11-29-2010)
4-7-11: REGULATION OF SOUND EQUIPMENT AND SOUND AMPLIFYING EQUIPMENT:
A.   No person shall use or cause to be used any loudspeaker, loudspeaker
system, sound amplifier, or any other machine or device which produces,
reproduces, or amplifies sound outside of buildings or other enclosed
structures for the purpose of amplifying a live performance or prerecorded
music without first obtaining a permit to do so.
B.   A permit may be obtained by making application to the city clerk or
designee.
C.   Application requests shall be filed with the city clerk. No application
request shall be accepted for filing and processing unless it conforms to the
requirements of this chapter, contains in a full, true, and correct form the
required materials and information prescribed by the forms supplied by the city
clerk and is accompanied by the appropriate fees.
D.   All permits are subject to approval by the city clerk or designee. The
city clerk shall have the discretion to refer any sound permit request to the
city council for their review and action. The city council must approve any
sound permit request that extends past ten o'clock (10:00) P.M. Before the city
decides to approve a sound permit request, the city may require the applicant
to provide notice, in a form and manner approved by the city clerk, of the
proposed event to all neighboring residential property owners located within
three hundred seventy feet (370') of the subject property.
E.   The permit requires separate payment for each type of activity and permits
shall be nontransferable. A permit for a single event or a series of events at
the same location may be issued. The city council, the city clerk, or designee
retains the ability to revoke or modify any issued permits for any alleged
violations of this chapter, including those based upon sound meter readings
taken by the city. The chief of police or designee may also terminate the
permit activity if the activity continues to exceed the maximum permitted sound
level after the permit holder or the holder's employee or agent has been
advised that the activity has exceeded the maximum permitted sound level.
F.   The permit shall be displayed on or immediately adjacent to the sound
equipment.
G.   Each application request shall be accompanied by the fee specified by city
council resolution before it is accepted for filing and processing.
H.   If the property is a rental property, the applicant needs to have written
permission from the landlord. If the property is under common ownership, the
applicant needs to have written permission from the landlord or association.
I.   The use of any loudspeaker, loudspeaker system, sound amplifier, or any
other similar machine or device which is permitted pursuant to this section is
subject to the following regulations:
1.   The only sound permitted shall be either music or human speech, or both.
2.   The volume of the sound amplified pursuant to this section shall not
exceed the maximum permissive sound levels measured from the receiving land
use, as outlined in this chapter.
J.   Any radio, record player, stereo, television, compact disc player, tape
deck or player, including any associated speakers, that is rated for fifty (50)
watts or less of electrical power does not require a sound permit application.
(Ord. 2053, 9-8-2014, eff. 1-1-2015)
4-7-12: CONDITIONS OF SOUND PERMIT APPROVAL:
A.   The city clerk or designee may regulate the issuance of a sound permit as
is necessary to meet the purposes of this chapter and protect the public
health, safety, and welfare of adjacent uses. Conditions which may be regulated
may include, but are not limited to:
1.   Setbacks.
2.   Fences, walls, or other screening necessary to mitigate noise.
3.   Control of noise, vibration, or other nuisances.
4.   Hours of operation. (Ord. 2053, 9-8-2014, eff. 1-1-2015)
4-7-13: PRIOR DETERMINATION FOR SOUND PERMIT APPROVAL:
A.   The following shall be considered in determination for approval of an
application for a sound permit:
1.   Adverse impact on the health, safety, and welfare of person or property in
the surrounding area.
2.   Prior violations of this chapter by the applicant requesting a sound
permit. (Ord. 1892, 11-29-2010)
4-7-14: APPEALS:
Wherein the applicant, the adjacent property owner, or any officer, department,
board, or bureau of the city is affected by any decision or order made by the
city clerk or designee regarding the approval or denial of a sound permit, such
appeal shall be taken within ten (10) calendar days from the decision or order
made by the city clerk or designee, by filing a written petition with the city
clerk requesting a hearing on the matter and specifying the grounds thereof. A
hearing before the municipal code hearing officer will be held as provided by
subsections
4-4-9E, F, and G of this title. An appeal pursuant to this chapter shall not
stay the effect of the decision or order made by the city clerk or designee
unless so ordered by the municipal code hearing officer. (Ord. 2053, 9-8-2014,
eff. 1-1-2015)
4-7-15: ENFORCEMENT:
The city clerk, the chief of police, or their designees are hereby designated
and ordered to enforce this chapter. The city clerk, the chief of police, or
their designees shall have primary but not exclusive enforcement responsibility
for this chapter. (Ord. 2053, 9-8-2014, eff. 1-1-2015)
4-7-16: PENALTIES:
Violations of this chapter are simple misdemeanors and are punishable by a fine
and/or a term of imprisonment as provided in section 903.1 of the code of Iowa
(2009). Violations of this chapter may also be punishable as municipal
infractions pursuant to title 1, chapter 4 of this code. Violations of section
4-7-7 of this chapter shall only be punishable as municipal infractions. The
chief of police or designees may issue criminal citations for violations. Any
individual(s) responsible for such violations, including property owners,
lessees, or any other person(s) occupying, maintaining, or managing the
property, may receive a criminal citation or be subject to a municipal
infraction. Each day that a violation occurs shall constitute a separate
offense. A two hundred fifty dollar ($250.00) civil penalty shall be imposed
for a first municipal infraction on the property at issue. A seven hundred
fifty dollar ($750.00) civil penalty shall be imposed for a second municipal
infraction within a twelve (12) month period on the property at issue. A one
thousand dollar ($1,000.00) civil penalty shall be imposed for a third or
subsequent municipal infraction within a twelve (12) month period on the
property at issue. Multiple violations of this chapter occurring on the
property at issue may be considered by the city for purposes of approving
licenses or for any other requirements that are subject to approval by the
city. The city may also seek to suspend or prohibit any sound related events or
activities on the property at issue once there have been three (3) or more
violations within a twelve (12) month period. (Ord. 1892, 11-29-2010)
CHAPTER 8
STORM WATER MANAGEMENT
ARTICLE A. SYSTEMS AND FACILITIES
SECTION:
4-8A-1: Purpose
4-8A-2: Definitions
4-8A-3: Scope And Responsibility For The Storm Water Utility
4-8A-4: Director Of Public Works
4-8A-5: Prohibited Acts
4-8A-6: Right Of Entry
4-8A-7: Penalties
4-8A-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this article is to establish a storm water utility which shall
be responsible for storm water management within the corporate boundaries of
the city of West Des Moines and shall provide for the management, protection,
control, regulation, use and enhancement of storm water management systems and
facilities. (Ord. 1683, 5-8-2006)
4-8A-2: DEFINITIONS:
The following terms are defined for use in this article, unless the context
specifically indicates otherwise:
COMMERCIAL/INDUSTRIAL: Any developed land whereon multiple-family dwellings,
commercial retail and office, industrial and manufacturing buildings, storage
buildings and storage areas covered with impervious surfaces, parking lots,
public and private school buildings, churches, hospitals and convalescent
centers have been constructed.
CUSTOMERS OF THE STORM WATER UTILITY: Include all persons, properties and
entities served by and/or benefiting from the utility's acquisition,
management, maintenance, extension and improvement of the public storm water
management systems and facilities.
DEVELOPED LAND: Land that has been altered from its natural state by
construction or installation of more than five hundred (500) square feet of
"impervious surface area" as defined herein.
DUPLEX DWELLING: A building containing only two (2) dwelling units and designed
for and occupied exclusively by not more than two (2) families with separate
housekeeping and cooking facilities for each. In the application of storm water
management fees, duplex dwelling properties shall be treated as two (2) single-
family dwellings.
EQUIVALENT RESIDENTIAL UNIT (ERU): The ERU shall be used as the basis for
determining storm water management fees. Less than or equal to four thousand
(4,000) square feet of impervious surface area shall be one ERU. Every
additional increment of one square foot to two thousand (2,000) square feet of
impervious surface area shall be one-half (0.5) ERU.
IMPERVIOUS SURFACE AREA: Those areas which prevent or impede the infiltration
of storm water into the soil as it enters in natural conditions prior to
development. Common impervious surface areas include, but are not limited to,
rooftops, sidewalks, driveways, patios, parking lots, storage areas, compacted
gravel surfaces and other surfaces which prevent or impede the natural
infiltration of storm water runoff which existed prior to development.
MULTIPLE-FAMILY DWELLING: A building or portion thereof containing more than
three (3) dwelling units designed for or occupied by more than three (3)
families with separate housekeeping and cooking facilities for each. In the
application of storm water management fees, multiple-family dwelling properties
shall be treated as commercial/industrial.
POLLUTANT: Anything that causes or contributes to pollution. Pollutants may
include, but are not limited to, paints, varnishes and solvents; oil and other
automotive fluids; nonhazardous liquid and solid wastes and yard wastes;
refuse, rubbish, garbage, litter or other discarded or abandoned objects, so
that the same may cause or contribute to pollution; pesticides, herbicides and
fertilizers; hazardous substances and wastes; sewage, fecal coliform bacteria
and pathogens; dissolved and particulate metals; animal wastes; waste and
residues that result from constructing a building or structure; and noxious or
offensive matter of any kind.
SINGLE-FAMILY DWELLING: A building containing only one dwelling unit and
designed for and occupied exclusively for residence purposes by only one
family.
STORM WATER MANAGEMENT FEES: The periodic rate, fee or charge applicable to a
parcel of developed land, which charge shall be reflective of the service
provided by the city of West Des Moines storm water utility. Storm water
management fees are based on measurable parameters which influence the storm
water utility's cost of providing services and facilities, with the most
important factor being the amount of impervious surface area on each parcel of
developed property. The storm water management fees shall be determined by
ordinance of the city council.
STORM WATER MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS AND FACILITIES: Storm water management systems
and facilities address the issue of drainage management (flooding) and
environmental quality (pollution, erosion and sedimentation) of receiving
rivers, streams, creeks, lakes and ponds through improvements, maintenance,
regulation and funding of plants, structures and property used in the
collection, retention, detention and treatment of storm water or surface water
drainage.
SUBSTANTIAL COMPLETION: The construction has been completed and the city of
West Des Moines has acknowledged that the construction has been completed in
accordance with the approved plans and specifications through the issuance of a
temporary certificate of occupancy or permanent certificate of occupancy.
TOWNHOME DWELLING: A dwelling unit which is detached or attached horizontally,
and not vertically, to one or more other dwelling units, wherein the land or
lot beneath each dwelling may be individually owned in common by a townhome
association. In the application of storm water management fees, each townhome
dwelling shall be treated as one single-family dwelling.
UNDEVELOPED LAND: Land in its unaltered natural state or which has been
modified to such minimal degree as to have a hydrologic response comparable to
land in an unaltered state shall be deemed undeveloped. Undeveloped land shall
have less than five hundred (500) square feet of pavement, asphalt or compacted
gravel surfaces or structures which create an impervious surface area that
would prevent infiltration of storm water or cause storm water to collect,
concentrate or flow in a manner materially different than that which would
