Connection fees are hereby established and shall be imposed upon owners of
properties within the Sugar Creek stormwater connection fee district, pursuant
to ordinance 2006, as follows:
A.   Fee Schedule: From the effective date through June 30, 2014, a connection
fee of four thousand seven hundred ten dollars ($4,710.00) per acre of property
served by the major stormwater drainage facilities shall be imposed.
Thereafter, the connection fee shall be annually adjusted as of July 1 of each
year according to ordinance 2006.
B.   Fee Outside District: The above established connection fee schedule shall
also apply to any properties located outside of the defined boundary of the fee
district from which the stormwater or overland flow drainage flows into the
boundary of the district and would be conveyed by one or more of the major
stormwater drainage facilities within the connection fee district.
C.   Exception: The above established connection fee schedule shall not apply
to any properties within the defined boundary of the fee district from which
stormwater or overland flow drainage does not flow into the boundary of the
district in such a manner that such flow would utilize one or more of the major
stormwater drainage facilities constructed within the district.
D.   Payment: The major stormwater drainage connection fee required by this
section shall be due and payable to the city treasurer.
1.   For property being platted the fee is due and payable before approval of
the final plat.
2.   For property subject to a site plan the fee is due and payable before
approval of the site plan.
3.   For all other property the fee is due and payable before issuance of a
building permit.
E.   Exemptions: The following properties shall be exempt from and not subject
to the connection fee:
1.   Platted lots with a single-family residential dwelling unit constructed
before, or under construction on, the effective date hereof; a single-family
residential unit would be considered under construction if an application for a
building permit is filed by June 30, 2014.
2.   Single-family residential dwellings on unplatted property constructed
before, or under construction on, the effective date hereof to a maximum area
of one acre.
3.   Platted property, developed or undeveloped, subject to an approved
development plan with the city on the effective date hereof establishing the
connection fee district for the area where the property is located.
4.   Nonresidential buildings on platted lots constructed before, or under
construction on, the effective date hereof, provided any future division of a
parcel shall subject the nondeveloped portion of the parcel to the connection
fee.
5.   Nonresidential development on an unplatted property constructed before, or
under construction on, the effective date hereof to the extent of the actual
developed area including buildings, drives, parking lots and other similar
types of surface improvements.
F.   Area Included: All properties shall be subject to the connection fee
district as follows:
1.   Newly Platted Property: The gross area of the plat less any street right
of way and area to be dedicated as public park.
2.   Site Plan: The gross area of the site plan less any street right of way,
area to be dedicated as public park and any area for which the connection fee
was previously paid.
3.   For Residential Development On A Previously Platted Area Of Less Than One
Acre: The gross area of the lot as proportioned to the per acre connection fee.
4.   For Residential Development On A Previously Platted Residential Parcel Of
More Than One Acre, Or Any Nonplatted Residential Parcel: One acre. The
property owner may designate the one acre single residence parcel and a
remainder parcel and the one acre single residence parcel shall be subject to
the connection fee. Any future development of said parcel shall necessitate a
revised application for connection and payment of the connection fee.
G.   Effect Of Schedule: The above connection fee schedule shall remain in
force and effect until such time that the city council adopts an ordinance to
adjust the connection fees to be imposed in subsequent years for the Sugar
Creek stormwater connection fee district. Nothing herein is intended to
restrict the city council from appropriate adjustment of the connection fee
schedule to reflect future construction costs.
H.   Major Stormwater Drainage Facilities Constructed: The city shall be
responsible to design and construct major stormwater drainage facilities within
the Sugar Creek stormwater connection fee district as graphically depicted on
exhibit B attached to the ordinance codified herein and on file in the office
of the city clerk. Other major stormwater drainage facilities to provide
comprehensive stormwater drainage to the Sugar Creek stormwater connection fee
district shall not be the responsibility of the city to design and construct
under the provisions of the Sugar Creek stormwater connection fee district.
I.   Previously Constructed Major Stormwater Drainage Facilities: Property
owners or their successors in interest who have constructed major stormwater
drainage improvements within the district prior to the effective date hereof
will be exempt from the connection fee if the value of the improvements
constructed exceeds the amount of the connection fee for that property owner's
parcel or parcels. To qualify, the previously constructed improvements must be
major stormwater drainage facilities that would have been included in the
calculation of the connection fee if that improvement was not previously
constructed. The connection fee district for the exempted property will be
reallocated for purposes of calculating the connection fee. This provision
shall be applicable only to major stormwater drainage improvements constructed
prior to the effective date hereof. (Ord. 2024, 4-7-2014)

Connection fees are hereby established and shall be imposed upon owners of
properties within the Grand Avenue East stormwater connection fee district,
pursuant to ordinance 2006, as follows:
A.   Fee Schedule: From the effective date through June 30, 2014, a connection
fee of fourteen thousand six hundred fifty four dollars ($14,654.00) per acre
of property served by the major stormwater drainage facilities shall be
imposed. Thereafter, the connection fee shall be annually adjusted as of July 1
of each year according to ordinance 2006.
B.   Fee Outside District: The above established connection fee schedule shall
also apply to any properties located outside of the defined boundary of the fee
district from which the stormwater or overland flow drainage flows into the
boundary of the district and would be conveyed by one or more of the major
stormwater drainage facilities within the connection fee district.
C.   Exception: The above established connection fee schedule shall not apply
to any properties within the defined boundary of the fee district from which
stormwater or overland flow drainage does not flow into the boundary of the
district in such a manner that such flow would utilize one or more of the major
stormwater drainage facilities constructed within the district.
D.   Payment: The major stormwater drainage connection fee required by this
section shall be due and payable to the city finance department.
1.   For property being platted the fee is due and payable before approval of
the final plat.
2.   For property subject to a site plan the fee is due and payable before
approval of the site plan.
3.   For all other property the fee is due and payable before issuance of a
building permit.
E.   Exemptions: The following properties shall be exempt from and not subject
to the connection fee:
1.   Platted lots with a single-family residential dwelling unit constructed
before, or under construction on the effective date hereof. A platted lot shall
be considered under construction on the effective date hereof if an application
for a building permit has been approved by June 30, 2014.
2.   Single-family residential dwellings on unplatted property constructed
before, or under construction on the effective date hereof to a maximum area of
one acre.
3.   Platted property, developed or undeveloped, subject to an approved
development plan with the city on the effective date hereof establishing the
connection fee district for the area where the property is located.
4.   Nonresidential buildings on platted lots constructed before, or under
construction on the effective date hereof, provided any future division of a
parcel shall subject the nondeveloped portion of the parcel to the connection
fee.
5.   Nonresidential development on an unplatted property constructed before, or
under construction on the effective date hereof to the extent of the actual
developed area, including buildings, drives, parking lots and other similar
types of surface improvements.
F.   Area Included: All properties shall be subject to the connection fee
district as follows:
1.   Newly Platted Property: The gross area of the plat less any street right
of way and area to be dedicated as public park.
2.   Site Plan: The gross area of the site plan less any street right of way
and area to be dedicated as public park, and any area for which the connection
fee was previously paid.
3.   For Residential Development On A Previously Platted Area Of Less Than One
Acre: The gross area of the lot as proportioned to the per acre connection fee.
4.   For Residential Development On A Previously Platted Residential Parcel Of
More Than One Acre, Or Any Nonplatted Residential Parcel: One acre. The
property owner may designate the one acre single residential parcel and a
remainder parcel, with the one acre single residential parcel subject to the
connection fee. Any future development of said parcel shall necessitate a
revised application for connection and payment of the connection fee.
G.   Effect Of Schedule: The above connection fee schedule shall remain in
force and effect until such time that the city council adopts an ordinance to
adjust the connection fees to be imposed in subsequent years for the Grand
Avenue East stormwater connection fee district. Nothing herein is intended to
restrict or prohibit the city council from appropriate adjustment of the
connection fee schedule to reflect future construction costs.
H.   Major Stormwater Drainage Facilities Constructed: The city shall be
responsible to design and construct major stormwater drainage facilities within
the Grand Avenue East stormwater connection fee district as graphically
depicted on exhibit B attached to the ordinance codified herein and on file in
the office of the city clerk. Other major stormwater drainage facilities to
provide comprehensive stormwater drainage to the Grand Avenue East stormwater
connection fee district shall not be the responsibility of the city to design
and construct under the provisions of the Grand Avenue East stormwater
connection fee district. (Ord. 2028, 4-21-2014)
CHAPTER 9
WATER SUPPLY PROTECTION
SECTION:
7-9-1: Purpose
7-9-2: Definitions
7-9-3: Protection for Publicly-Owned Shallow Wells
7-9-4: Protection for Publicly-Owned Deep Wells
7-9-5: Applicability of Provisions
7-9-6: Existing Structures and Facilities
7-9-1: PURPOSE:
It is the purpose of this Chapter to protect the public water supply of the
City by regulating the locations and types of construction of certain
structures or facilities which may be potential sources of contamination of the
publicly-owned water supply wells. (Ord. 944, 3-4-91)
7-9-2: DEFINITIONS:
The definitions of words used herein shall be those found in textbooks of Civil
Engineering, except a shallow well is a well located and constructed in such a
manner that there is not a continuous layer of low permeability soil or rock
(or equivalent retarding mechanism acceptable to the department) at least 5
feet thick, the top of which is located at least 25 feet below the normal
ground surface and above the aquifer from which water is to be drawn. (Ord.
944, 3-4-91; amd. Ord. 2406, 3-2-2020)
7-9-3: PROTECTION FOR PUBLICLY-OWNED SHALLOW WELLS:
No structure or facility shall be located within the distances as outlined in
the Iowa Administrative Code 567 Chapter 43 , from a publicly-owned shallow
well within the City. (Ord. 2406, 3-2-2020)
7-9-4: PROTECTION FOR PUBLICLY-OWNED DEEP WELLS:
No structure or facility shall be located within the distances as outlined in
the Iowa Administrative Code 567 Chapter 43, from a publicly-owned deep well
within the City. (Ord. 2406, 3-2-2020)
7-9-5: APPLICABILITY OF PROVISIONS:
The provisions of this Chapter shall apply to all publicly-owned wells existing
within the City, except former publicly-owned wells which have been abandoned
and from which the pumping equipment has been removed. (Ord. 944, 3-4-91)
7-9-6: EXISTING STRUCTURES AND FACILITIES:
The use of structures and facilities existing on the effective date hereof may
be continued even though such use may not conform with the regulations of this
Chapter. Such structure shall not be enlarged, extended, reconstructed or
substituted subsequent to the effective date hereof. (Ord. 944, 3-4-91)
CHAPTER 10
TREES AND SHRUBS
SECTION:
7-10-1: Purpose
7-10-2: Definitions
7-10-3: Authority Of The Code Enforcement Officer
7-10-4: Authority Of The City Forester
7-10-5: Duties Of The City Forester
7-10-6: Permit Required
7-10-7: General Standards
7-10-8: Unauthorized Interference With Public Trees And Shrubs
7-10-9: Insurance And Bond For Businesses Engaged In Working With Trees And
Shrubs
7-10-10: Violation Notice And Assessment
7-10-11: Appeal
7-10-12: Protection Of Trees
7-10-13: Interference With The City Forester, Code Enforcement Officer, Or City
Employees Enforcing This Chapter
7-10-14: Penalties
7-10-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this chapter is to promote and protect the public health,
safety, and general welfare and to preserve the benefits provided by trees by
providing for the regulation of the planting, maintenance, and removal of trees
and shrubs within the city. (Ord. 2083, 2-23-2015)
7-10-2: DEFINITIONS:
For use in this chapter, the following terms are defined:
CITY FORESTER: The city manager or any person designated by the city manager of
the city of West Des Moines to enforce this chapter.
CLOSING: A closing exists any time the movement of pedestrian or vehicular
traffic shall be stopped on a public way, for reason of public safety, as a
result of any action covered by this chapter.
CODE ENFORCEMENT OFFICER: The city manager or any enforcement officer
designated by the city manager of the city of West Des Moines to enforce this
chapter.
NUISANCE: Whatever is injurious to health, public safety, indecent, or
offensive to the senses, or an obstruction to the free use of property so as to
unreasonably interfere with the enjoyment of life or property.
PERSONS: An individual, firm, partnership, domestic or foreign corporation,
company, association, trust, or legal entity.
PROPERTY OWNER: A person owning or responsible for private property in the
city.
PUBLIC PROPERTY: Any and all property not defined as public right of way (ROW)
located within the confines of the city and owned by the city of West Des
Moines, Iowa, or held in the name of the city by any of the departments,
commissions, or agencies within the city government.
PUBLIC RIGHT OF WAY (ROW): All the land lying between property lines on either
side of all public streets, alleys, and boulevards or parkways, including
public easements and grants to the city of West Des Moines, Iowa. The term used
herein shall include vertical directions above and below the ground surface
within the public right of way.
PUBLIC TREE OR SHRUB: Any perennial woody plant, shrub, or tree located on
public right of way or public property of the city of West Des Moines.
PUBLIC UTILITY COMPANY: Includes purveyors of electricity, natural gas, water,
telephone, communications services and cable television services, and storm and
sanitary sewer facilities, who are governmental agencies, who are performing
services related to city initiated public improvement projects, or who have a
valid franchise to operate within the city of West Des Moines.
SHRUB: Any woody perennial plant less than fifteen feet (15') tall at maturity,
multiple stemmed, and adaptable to shaping, trimming, and pruning without
injury.
TREE: Any woody perennial plant greater than fifteen feet (15') at maturity.
(Ord. 2083, 2-23-2015)
7-10-3: AUTHORITY OF THE CODE ENFORCEMENT OFFICER:
The code enforcement officer shall have the authority to enforce nuisance
abatement of trees and shrubs growing on private property which violate city
ordinances or policies. (Ord. 2083, 2-23-2015)
7-10-4: AUTHORITY OF THE CITY FORESTER:
The city forester shall have the authority to perform and to regulate the
planting, maintenance, and removal of public trees and shrubs. The city
forester shall manage public trees and shrubs in order to promote and protect
public health, safety, and general welfare and to preserve the benefits of city
tree resources. The city forester shall enforce nuisance abatement of trees and
shrubs growing on public property which violate city ordinances or policies.
(Ord. 2083, 2-23-2015)
7-10-5: DUTIES OF THE CITY FORESTER:
The city forester shall have and exercise the following duties pertaining to
public trees and shrubs:
A.   Pruning Or Removal: To prevent indiscriminate pruning or removal of public
trees and shrubs.
B.   New Plantings: To regulate and locate new plantings of public trees and
shrubs in accordance with the "City Forestry Standards Of Practice And
Specifications".
C.   Secure Compliance: To order persons to comply with the duties placed upon
them by this chapter.
D.   Advise: To assist and advise code enforcement officers and other city
employees regarding trees and shrubs on public and private property.
E.   Supervision: To supervise all activities by city employees and contractors
in the planting, maintenance, and removal of public trees and shrubs. To
supervise does not require the city forester to be physically present to
directly monitor such activities.
F.   Issue Permits: To issue all tree and shrub permits in accordance with
section
7-10-6 of this chapter.
G.   Conditions Of Permit: To affix reasonable conditions to the granting of a
permit hereunder and supervise work done under the permit.
H.   Replacement Of Public Trees And Shrubs For Public Improvement: If
replacement of public trees or shrubs is required, it shall occur within one
hundred twenty (120) calendar days after the public improvement has been
completed, or within the appropriate planting season at the discretion of the
city forester.
I.   Removal Of Trees Or Shrubs For Nuisance Abatement: To remove or require
removal of any public tree or shrub in whole or part that is so hazardous,
diseased, or insect ridden as to be deemed a nuisance.
J.   Notification Of Future Tree Or Shrub Removal On Public Property: To
provide written notification via certified mail with return receipt requested
and regular mail to the abutting property owner at least fourteen (14) calendar
days prior to any scheduled removal. Unclaimed or returned mail shall not
constitute improper notification. The notification shall provide that the
abutting property owner must contact the city within fourteen (14) calendar
days of the date of the mailing if the property owner has any questions or
concerns regarding the tree or shrub removal. Notification shall not be
required for the removal of a public tree or shrub in an emergency situation as
determined by the city forester. Notification shall also not be required if the
abutting property owner requested the removal of the public tree or shrub. No
right is conferred upon or provided to the abutting property owner due to
notification of removal. (Ord. 2083, 2-23-2015)
7-10-6: PERMIT REQUIRED:
No person shall plant, remove, treat, prune, cable, brace, or otherwise disturb
a public tree or shrub without first applying for and receiving a permit from
the city forester. Requests for permits must be made a minimum of forty eight
(48) business hours in advance of the time the work shall begin. A permit will
not be required to prune branches that are less than six inches (6") in
diameter. All work shall be performed in accordance with the "City Forestry
Standards Of Practice And Specifications". The city shall be exempt from
acquiring permits to perform necessary maintenance to public trees and shrubs
or to remove public trees and shrubs as part of a city initiated public
improvement project. Property owners shall be exempt from acquiring permits for
planting, removing, or otherwise disturbing a public tree or shrub if the work
is being performed as part of a development agreement approved by the city. If
being performed as part of a development agreement, the city forester shall be
notified a minimum of forty eight (48) business hours in advance of the time
the work shall begin.
A.   Required Permits And Ensuing Conditions Of Issuance: The following permits
with the ensuing conditions of issuance shall be obtained before any private
person or entity performs any work on public trees and shrubs:
1.   Planting: A permit shall be issued for planting within the public right of
way or on public property when the city forester finds that the new planting is
desirable and the method of workmanship will be satisfactory and that the new
planting(s) will conform to the "City Forestry Standards Of Practice And
Specifications". A permit shall be denied if the planting(s) will likely create
a future public nuisance or danger. Any tree planted within the public right of
way or on public property pursuant to this chapter shall become the property of
the city.
2.   Removal: A permit shall be issued for removal of a public tree or shrub,
including where the city forester finds the tree or shrub interferes with
performing improvements within the public right of way or on public property,
or the tree or shrub creates a public nuisance or danger. All public tree or
shrub removal shall conform to the "City Forestry Standards Of Practice And
Specifications".
No person shall close any street, alley, boulevard or parkway, highway,
sidewalk, or trail to remove a public tree or shrub or private tree, or any
portion thereof, without first obtaining the approval for such closing from the
city in writing.
3.   Treatment: A permit shall be issued for the treatment of any tree located
within the public right of way for disease or insect infestation. A permit will
only be issued when the tree has been designated by the city forester as a
candidate for possible treatment. When required by law, treatment shall be
performed by a commercial pesticide applicator licensed to perform work in the
state of Iowa and shall consist of chemical treatments approved by the city
forester.
B.   Permits; Contents Of Permit Application: The application shall be made on
a form supplied by the city. A fee may be assessed for the permit to cover the
cost of administration. Fees will be established by resolution of the city
council. Fees will not be required from public agencies or franchised utilities
that operate within the city. The applicant shall, at the time of making the
application, agree in writing to, in all respects, save the city harmless,
indemnify the city, and protect the city and the public at all times in
connection with work done under such permit.
C.   Inspection Of Location Designated By The Permit: The city forester shall
inspect the location designated by the permit, and if in his or her opinion it
will be desirable that such tree or shrub be planted, removed, treated, or
otherwise disturbed, the city forester shall issue a permit.
D.   Improper Planting: Trees and shrubs planted within the public right of way
or on public property without authorization or in accordance with an issued
permit, and public trees and shrubs found growing in violation of the "City
Forestry Standards Of Practice And Specifications", are subject to removal by
the city forester following the appropriate notification.
E.   Utility Requirements: All public utilities, their agents, employees, and
subcontractors shall operate under an annual permit to prune public trees and
shrubs for the purpose of eliminating potential hazards to public safety, to
maintain their facilities, and to install or replace existing utilities. The
annual permit requirement shall not apply to City initiated public improvement
projects. The utility company shall provide to the City Forester a copy of its
work specifications and work schedule a minimum of forty eight (48) business
hours prior to the commencement of any work. In cases of emergency,
notification shall be given a maximum of forty eight (48) hours after the
commencement of work. All work must comply with the "City Forestry Standards of
Practice and Specifications". (Ord. 2083, 2-23-2015)
7-10-7: GENERAL STANDARDS:
Any person growing a tree or shrub on private property, or growing a tree,
shrub, garden, or other vegetative growth, or installing landscaping,
structures, or other objects located within private property which encroaches
upon the public right- of-way or that interferes with the vision triangle as
provided in this Code, or any person growing a public tree or shrub, shall
comply with the following standards:
A.   Maintenance: Trees or shrubs planted within the public right- of-way that
extend over public streets or sidewalks, or that obstruct traffic signs or
public utilities, shall be maintained by the City. Trees or shrubs planted on
private property that extend over public streets or sidewalks, or obstruct
traffic signs or public utilities, shall be maintained by owners of abutting
property in accordance with this section and the "City Forestry Standards of
Practice and Specifications" at the cost of the property owner. Maintenance
includes, but is not limited to, watering, fertilizing, insect and disease
control, treatment, and pruning. The City reserves the right to perform
maintenance of private or public trees or shrubs that are planted or extend
into the public right-of-way without notice or compensation to the abutting
property owner if the City Forester determines that such maintenance is
necessary to promote and protect the public health, safety, and general
welfare.
B.   Pruning: Subject to the maintenance responsibility provisions cited above,
trees or shrubs shall be properly pruned for the purpose of preventing the
following potentially hazardous situations: the obstruction of traffic signs;
the obstruction of a clear view of street and alley intersections; the
obstruction of the proper lighting of public streets and places; and the
obstruction of public walks, trails, or streets. The minimum vertical clearance
of trees and shrubs shall be fourteen feet (14') between the surface of a
street and the lowest branch. The minimum vertical clearance shall be eight
feet (8') between the surface of a sidewalk, trail, or other pedestrian way and
the lowest branch. All pruning shall be done in accordance with the "City
Forestry Standards of Practice and Specifications".
C.   Avoid Damage Or Nuisance: The planting of trees, shrubs, gardens, or other
vegetative growth, or the installation of landscaping, structures, or other
objects on private property which would cause a public danger or nuisance shall
be prohibited.
D.   Street Or Alley Intersection: The planting of trees, shrubs, gardens, or
other vegetative growth, or the installation of landscaping, structures, or
other objects on corner lots or lots adjacent to an alley within the area
bounded by street or alley lines of such lots and a line joining points along
said street or alley lines twenty five feet (25') from the point of
intersection of the public right-of-way lines, defined in this Code as the
"vision triangle", shall be limited to trees, shrubs, gardens, and other
vegetative growth, and landscaping, structures, and other objects located
within this area that shall not exceed two feet (2') in height, and the lowest
branches of any trees planted outside of this area, but the branches of such
trees that extend within this area, must be a minimum of ten feet (10') in
height. Height shall be measured from the curb elevation and trees, shrubs,
gardens, and other vegetative growth must be pruned or maintained to comply
with these height restrictions to create an unobstructed view of the
intersection between heights of two feet (2') and ten feet (10') above the curb
elevation. Notwithstanding these height restrictions, no trees, shrubs,
gardens, or other vegetative growth shall be planted within the vision triangle
that create or constitute a vision obstruction to vehicular, bicycle, or
pedestrian traffic. Similarly, no landscaping, structures, or other objects
shall be placed within the vision triangle that create or constitute a vision
obstruction to vehicular, bicycle, or pedestrian traffic. The City shall have
sole discretion to determine whether a vision obstruction exists for vehicular,
bicycle, and pedestrian traffic. There shall be no compensation by the City to
the affected property owner for any damage to or removal of any trees, shrubs,
gardens, or other vegetative growth, or any damage to or removal of
landscaping, structures, or other objects, encroaching upon the public right-
of-way or that interferes with the "vision triangle" as defined in this Code.
E.   Dead, Diseased, Or Insect Ridden Trees Or Shrubs: Dead, diseased, or
insect ridden trees or shrubs shall be subject to the following conditions:
1.   Public Trees Or Shrubs: The City Forester shall coordinate treatment or
removal of any public tree or shrub which is so hazardous, diseased or insect
ridden as to be deemed a nuisance and constitutes a hazard to other trees or
shrubs or the public safety. Public trees that are at risk of becoming diseased
or insect ridden may be treated or preemptively removed by the City as part of
a management plan approved by the City Council. Trees in the public right-of-
way not identified for treatment by the City and not deemed a nuisance or a
hazard may be treated by the abutting property owner with an approved permit.
2.   Trees Or Shrubs Located Within Private Property: The Code Enforcement
Officer shall provide written notice to be served on a property owner by
personal service, or by certified mail with return receipt requested and
regular mail, requiring the treatment or removal within fourteen (14) calendar
days of notification of any trees or shrubs located within private property
which are dead, diseased or insect ridden so as to be deemed a nuisance and
constitute a hazard to public trees or shrubs, other trees or shrubs on private
property, or public safety. Such removal, pruning, or treatment as required by
provisions of this section shall be subject to the applicable "City Forestry
Standards of Practice and Specifications".
F.   Prohibited Trees: Trees prohibited from being planted within public
property shall be identified by the City Forester and included on an official
list. Copies of this list shall be made available at City offices and on the
City website.
G.   Appropriate Trees: Any tree planted in the public right-of-way must first
meet all requirements listed in the City's tree planting permit. Trees
appropriate to be planted within the public right-of-way are those listed in
the most recent edition of Iowa State University's extension bulletin Pm-1429e
"Street Trees" and Pm-1429d "Low-Growing Trees for Urban and Rural Iowa".
Copies of these lists are available at City offices and through the Polk County
Extension Office. Other trees or shrubs not listed within these publications,
but not prohibited, may be reviewed and approved at the discretion of the City
Forester. (Ord. 2192, 12-27-2016)
7-10-8: UNAUTHORIZED INTERFERENCE WITH PUBLIC TREES AND SHRUBS:
The following actions are prohibited on public trees and shrubs unless
authorized by the City Forester:
A.   Damage: Damaging, cutting, carving, transplanting, or removing any public
tree or shrub.
B.   Attachments: Attaching any rope, wire, nails, or other contrivance to any
public tree or shrub.
C.   Electric Wire: Causing or permitting any wire charged with electricity to
come in contact with any public tree or shrub.
D.   Harmful Substance: Allowing any gaseous, liquid, or solid substance which
is harmful to any public tree or shrub to come in contact with it or the soil
supporting the sustenance of any public tree or shrub.
E.   Fire: Setting fire or permitting any fire to burn when such fire or the
heat thereof will injure any portion of any public tree or shrub.
F.   Exception: Fastening holiday or ornamental lighting from November 1 to
January 15 is allowed. (Ord. 2083, 2-23-2015)
7-10-9: INSURANCE AND BOND FOR BUSINESSES ENGAGED IN WORKING WITH TREES AND
SHRUBS:
A.   Insurance: Any person or entity engaging in the business of trimming,
pruning, spraying, or otherwise treating trees or shrubs on private property
within the City shall be sufficiently insured and bonded at all times the
person or entity performs these services. Any person or entity engaging in the
business of trimming, pruning, spraying, or otherwise treating trees or shrubs
on public property within the City shall acquire, and continuously maintain
during the period in which the person or entity is performing services, and
shall provide the City with acceptable proof of liability insurance coverage
that satisfies the City's requirements.
For the trimming, pruning, spraying, or otherwise treating trees or shrubs on
public property by others, the City shall be named as an additional insured by
endorsement to the liability insurance policy. Certificates of insurance
evidencing that the person or entity has secured the required liability
insurance must be provided to the City prior to the commencement of any work. A
minimum of thirty (30) calendar days' notice to the City prior to the
cancellation of or change in any such insurance shall be endorsed on each
policy and noted on each certificate.
B.   Bond: A bond or cash deposit in the amount of five thousand dollars
($5,000.00) shall be deposited with the City to assure adequate cleanup of
activities. (Ord. 2083, 2-23-2015)
7-10-10: VIOLATION NOTICE AND ASSESSMENT:
If a person or property owner is in violation of any regulations of this
chapter, the Code Enforcement Officer or City Forester may serve written notice
on the responsible person by personal service, or by certified mail with return
receipt requested and regular mail; or if the certified mail is returned
undelivered, then by posting a copy of said notice at the address of the
responsible person. The notice shall include a sufficiently detailed
description of the violation and shall allow a reasonable time for the
performance of any required remedial actions or order to cease and desist all
work regulated by this chapter. If the responsible person or property owner
fails to undertake the remedial actions specified in the notice within the
allowable time, the Code Enforcement Officer or City Forester may take steps to
effect compliance with the violation, to revoke any applicable permit, to
perform the required action, and to assess the reasonable costs to the
responsible person or property owner and against the private property for
collection in the same manner as Property Tax. (Ord. 2083, 2-23-2015)
7-10-11: APPEAL:
A.   Any appeal of a decision of the Code Enforcement Officer or City Forester
shall be submitted in writing to the Code Enforcement Officer or City Forester
within ten (10) calendar days of the date the City personally served or mailed
the notice. Fees for appeal shall be established by resolution of the City
Council. The subject matter of an appeal may be the issuance of permits under
this chapter, the concurrence of the City Forester in permits required under
other ordinances or policies, violation notices issued by the Code Enforcement
Officer or City Forester, or other relevant matters involving the
interpretation and enforcement of this chapter.
B.   The appeal shall be considered by the City Manager or designee within
thirty (30) calendar days of receiving the appeal. Action by the Code
Enforcement Officer or City Forester shall be stayed until the decision of the
City Manager or designee is rendered, unless the Code Enforcement Officer or
City Forester certifies to the City Manager or designee, after notice of appeal
shall have been filed with him or her, that by reason of the facts stated in
the petition, a stay would, in his or her opinion, cause imminent peril to life
or property. In such a case, proceedings shall not be stayed unless an
injunction has been obtained from a court of record.
C.   The City Manager or designee may reverse, affirm, modify, or waive, wholly
or partially, any decision of the Code Enforcement Officer or City Forester, or
the City Manager or designee may grant, deny, or revoke any permit or license.
The decision of the City Manager or designee shall be final. (Ord. 2083, 2-23-
2015)
7-10-12: PROTECTION OF TREES:
All public trees and shrubs deemed to be saved during construction or
reconstruction activities shall be protected by the developer or property owner
from damages or disturbances, including their root systems. Protective fences
shall be placed and maintained at or beyond the drip line of public trees and
shrubs that are unaffected by approved excavation or construction activities,
but are subject to damage during said activities. Any disturbance of any kind
within the fenced area shall be prohibited. Cutting, boring, and filling soil
within the drip line of a public tree or shrub to be preserved shall be
prohibited unless otherwise approved by the City Forester. Soil compaction
caused by any type of equipment shall not be allowed to occur over the
protected area of the root zone of any public tree or shrub unless approved by
the City Forester. (Ord. 2083, 2-23-2015)
7-10-13: INTERFERENCE WITH THE CITY FORESTER, CODE ENFORCEMENT OFFICER, OR CITY
EMPLOYEES ENFORCING THIS CHAPTER:
It is unlawful for any person or property owner to hinder, obstruct, or
otherwise interfere with the City Forester, Code Enforcement Officer, or
employees of the City while engaged in carrying out the provisions of this
chapter. (Ord. 2083, 2-23-2015)
7-10-14: PENALTIES:
The following penalties shall be imposed upon any person or property owner who
violates any provision of this chapter:
A.   Any person or property owner who violates the provisions of this chapter,
upon conviction, shall be punished as set forth in title 1, chapter 4 of this
Code.
B.   In addition to the penalties provided above, any person or property owner
found guilty of violating the provisions of this chapter may be required to pay
the cost of repair or replacement of such public tree or shrub. The replacement
costs shall be determined in accordance with the latest version of "A Guide for
Plant Appraisal" as published by the International Society of Arboriculture and
authored by the Council of Tree and Landscape Appraisers.
C.   The City reserves the right to collect costs in addition to penalties. The
imposition of any penalty of a violation of this chapter shall not be construed
as a waiver of the right of the City to collect the costs of removal or
treatment of any tree or shrub in accordance with the provisions of this
chapter.
D.   Public utilities may be held responsible for the replacement of any public
tree or shrub which has been severely damaged or died in the opinion of the
City Forester as a result of the maintenance or new installation of utilities.
The City Forester shall coordinate with the public utility appropriate and
reasonable replacement of said severely damaged or dead public tree or shrub in
accordance with the "City Forestry Standards of Practice and Specifications".
E.   Property owners abutting the area on which the public tree or shrub is
located shall be notified by the utility company forty eight (48) hours prior
to the commencement of any utility repair, maintenance, or replacement
activities which will affect or harm the public tree or shrub. In cases of
emergency repair, the City Forester shall have the option to waive said
notification. (Ord. 2083, 2-23-2015)
CHAPTER 11
PARK REGULATIONS
SECTION:
7-11-1: Purpose
7-11-2: Rules And Regulations
7-11-3: Penalty
7-11-1: PURPOSE:
The city council has adopted certain park rules governing the use of and
conduct in city parks. The term “city park(s)” as used herein refers to the
city parks, park facilities within city parks, and trails within city parks
located within or without the corporation limits of the city. The term “parks
and recreation facility” as used herein refers to a facility owned or operated
by the City of West Des Moines including, but not limited to, Raccoon River
Park Nature Lodge, Valley Junction Activity Center, Raccoon River Park Softball
Complex, Holiday Park Baseball Complex, MidAmerican Energy RecPlex, Raccoon
River Park Boathouse, and Jamie Hurd Amphitheater. The term “greenways” as used
herein refers to designated open spaces, typically located along a natural
corridor, that are preserved for environmental protection or recreational use
such as street-separated recreational trails. (Ord. 1355, 3-22-1999; amd. Ord.
2438, 9-8-2020; Ord. 2649, 1-21-2025)
7-11-2: RULES AND REGULATIONS:
The following rules and regulations are established concerning the conduct and
use of city parks and parks and recreation facilities, also regulating traffic
and parking automobiles and vehicles. Persons and vehicles authorized for
activities related to public safety or maintenance are exempt from the
regulations:
A.   Use Of Roadways: No person shall ride or drive any automobile, motorcycle,
moped, snowmobile or any other motorized vehicle in any city park or parks and
recreation facility except on the established roads or designated areas.
B.   Speed: No person shall ride or drive any automobile or other vehicle in a
city park or parks and recreation facility at a speed in excess of fifteen (15)
miles per hour.
C.   Parking: Vehicles shall be parked in designated parking lots and marked
stalls only, unless the parks and recreation director or designee has
specifically authorized parking on the grass or outside designated parking
lots. No vehicle shall be parked or allowed to remain within any city park or
parks and recreation facility overnight or outside posted hours unless
specifically authorized by the parks and recreation director or designee. No
person(s) shall obstruct or impede the normal flow of traffic within a city
park or parks and recreation facility.
D.   Hitching Animals: No person shall ride a horse or other animal or operate
any type of horse or animal drawn conveyance in a city park or parks and
recreation facility except by permission of the director of parks and
recreation or designee.
E.   Destruction Of Natural Environment: No person shall in any manner deface,
injure or remove any tree, shrub, or plant standing or growing in a city park
or parks and recreation facility or pick or destroy flowers or seeds growing
therein, or remove nests or wildlife/wildfowl.
F.   Fires: No fires shall be lighted or made in any city park or parks and
recreation facility except with the permission of the director of parks and
recreation or designee, provided that this subsection does not apply to fires
in stoves, ovens, grills, fire rings or fireplaces provided in any city park or
parks and recreation facility for use in picnic cooking. Fires may be
prohibited entirely during posted periods.
G.   Firearms, Weapons, Or Explosives: No person shall use firearms,
explosives, weapons, firecrackers or fireworks in any city park or parks and
recreation facility except as otherwise provided by any other section of this
code. Fireworks displays may be allowed by permission of the director of parks
and recreation and the fire chief.
H.   Litter: No person shall deposit upon or litter the ground with any form of
waste material in any city park or parks and recreation facility. All waste
shall be deposited in receptacles provided for such purposes.
I.   Use Of Tobacco: No person, at any time, shall use tobacco of any kind
while present on any city park or parks and recreation facility property.
Tobacco includes any product made or derived from tobacco that is intended for
human use, including any component, part, or accessory of a tobacco product.
This includes, but is not limited to, cigarettes, electronic smoking devices,
cigarette tobacco, roll your own tobacco, smokeless tobacco, and dissolvable
tobacco. "Electronic smoking devices" means any device that can be used to
deliver an aerosolized solution that may or may not contain nicotine to the
person inhaling from the device, including, but not limited to, an e-cigarette,
e-cigar, e-pipe, vape pen, e-hookah, or other simulated smoking device.
Nicotine products approved by the United States food and drug administration
for tobacco cessation shall be allowed within city parks.
J.   Defacing Of Public Property: No person shall write, mark or draw
characters on or deface, injure or destroy any building, or part thereof, or
improvement, apparatus or fixture, wall or fence, drain or sewer located on or
in any city park or parks and recreation facility.
K.   Posted Notices: (Rep. by Ord. 1197, 9-9-1996)
L.   Control Of Animals: The parks and recreation department may establish
policies for parks and recreation facilities regarding animals. All animals in
a city park or where allowed in a parks and recreation facility must be under
the control of a person competent to restrain and control the animal, either by
leash, cord, chain, or other similar restraint not more than ten feet (10') in
length, or properly restrained within a motor vehicle. The owner or person in
charge of an animal shall clean up and/or remove as soon as possible any
excrement or droppings deposited by the animal on city park or parks and
recreation facility property.
The requirement of a restraint on an animal shall not apply to animals
registered to use a designated off-leash area of a city park while in said off-
leash area and while abiding by all the rules and regulations of such
designated off leash area.
M.   Hours: No person shall be in any city park, between the hours of ten
thirty o’clock (10:30) P.M. to six o’clock (6:00) A.M. or at any time duly
posted and designated by the director of parks and recreation.
Exceptions: Authorized users of Raccoon River Park Nature Lodge and Raccoon
River Park Softball Complex are exempt from the hours restriction when using
their respective parks and recreation facility.
N.   Safety: (Rep. by Ord. 1197, 9-9-1996)
O.   Compliance With Rules: All persons shall abide by rules established by
city ordinance or by the parks and recreation department and posted in city
parks and parks and recreation facilities.
P.   Posting: No person shall post, fasten, paint or affix any placard, bill,
notice or sign upon any structure, tree, stone, directional sign, fence or
enclosure along or within any city park or parks and recreation facility except
by permission of the director of parks and recreation.
Q.   Moving Fixtures: (Rep. by Ord. 1197, 9-9-1996)
R.   Grounds Alteration: No person shall cut or remove any wood, turf, grass,
soil, rock, sand or gravel from any city park or parks and recreation facility
without written permission from the director of parks and recreation.
S.   Consumption of Alcohol: The department of parks and recreation may
establish facility use policies regarding alcoholic beverage possession,
consumption, and sales within parks and recreation facilities. No person shall
consume an alcoholic beverage as defined by Iowa Code (2020) while present upon
Holiday Aquatic Center premises, Valley View Aquatic Center premises, the
designated beach and swimming area at Raccoon River Park, Crossroads Park,
Western Hills Park, Brookview Park, Woodland Hills Park, Maple Grove Park, or
on any trail, parking lot, driveway, or road within a city park or parking lot
providing parking for any parks and recreation facility. However, beer, high
alcohol content beer, wine, and canned cocktails as defined by the Iowa Code
(2020) may be possessed and consumed in any other city park owned or leased by
the city, provided it is within individual cans not exceeding sixteen (16)
ounces in size. Dispensing from kegs shall be permitted only with written
permission of the director under the policy adopted by the department for the
park and recreation facility or during activities held pursuant to a city
special event permit. Signs prohibiting the consumption or possession of
alcoholic beverages shall be posted where appropriate.
T.   Responsibility Of Adults: (Rep. by Ord. 1197, 9-9-1996)
U.   Park Roads: No city park road shall be used as a through street by any
vehicle where posted.
V.   Golfing: No person shall play or practice golf in any city park or parks
and recreation facility, except during supervised activities approved by the
director of parks and recreation.
W.   Prohibited Activities: The following activities are specifically
prohibited in any city park or parks and recreation facility:
1   Disposing Of Material: No person shall place, store or dump any organic or
inorganic materials including raked leaves, grass clippings, compost,
construction material, firewood, paint, trash, debris, junk or any similar
materials in city dumpsters or on city park or parks and recreation facility
property.
2   Private Improvements: No person shall garden, mow or plant trees without
written permission from the department of parks and recreation. No person shall
install other private improvements such as fences, play equipment, irrigation
systems, or similar encroachments on city park.
3   Miscellaneous: No person shall remove or deposit snow on city park or parks
and recreation facility property. No person shall bury animals on city park or
parks and recreation facility property. No glass bottles shall be allowed in
city parks or where prohibited by parks and recreation facility policy.
The parks and recreation department is authorized to monitor and enforce such
rules and regulations. Enforcement procedures shall follow city code procedures
for either administrative abatement or municipal infraction as determined in
the best interest of the city.
X.   Swimming/Beach Use: Swimming shall be allowed in posted areas only, except
for organized activities approved by the director of parks and recreation. No
swimming shall be allowed from boats. Inner tubes, air mattresses, or other
beach toy type items shall be allowed in posted areas only.
Y.   Ice Skating: Ice skating shall be allowed in posted areas only. Ice
skating shall only be allowed when posted as safe.
Z.   Boating: A boat equipped with any size motor may be operated at a no wake
speed on Blue Heron Lake, except for in areas designated as "Non-Motorized And
Electric Motors Only" zones. All other regulations under the code of Iowa,
chapter 462A, shall apply. All sailboats with a mast height measuring thirty-
six feet (36') or greater above the water surface are prohibited on the Blue
Heron Lake. Additionally, all sailboats are prohibited on Blue Heron Lake when
the lake water level reaches an elevation of one foot (1') above the concrete
dock at the boat ramp.
AA.   Fishing: Fishing activities in parks shall comply with the code of Iowa,
chapter 481A.
BB.   Sales In Parks: No sales activities or admissions shall be allowed in any
city park except with approval of the director of parks and recreation or in
accordance with parks and recreation facility policies.
CC.   Hunting: It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in any hunting
activity on city park or parks and recreation facility property using a rifle,
shotgun, bow and arrow or any other means on land or in the water unless
approved by official action of the park and recreation advisory board and the
city council.
DD.   Trapping; Exceptions: It shall be unlawful for any person to place,
locate, set, use or attempt to use on city park or parks and recreation
facility property, any type of claw, spring or metal trap of any nature on land
or in the water, or to set, use or maintain any snare, pitfall, deadfall,
spring gun, set gun or device of similar character or purpose.
Exceptions: The city or its authorized agents are exempt from the above and may
control or manage animals, birds, or insects pursuant to established policies
that have been approved by the city council.
EE.   Camping: All overnight camping in city parks or parks and recreation
facilities is prohibited unless written authorization is received from the
director of parks and recreation. (Ord. 1355, 3-22-1999; amd. Ord. 1360, 5-3-
1999; Ord. 1566, 1-5-2004; Ord. 2022, 2-24-2014; Ord. 2104, 7-13-2015; Ord.
2140, 3-21-2016; Ord. 2438, 9-8-2020; Ord. 2649, 1-21-2025)
7-11-3: PENALTY:
Violations of this chapter are declared to be municipal infractions and may be
punished as provided in title 1, chapter 4 of this code. For violations of
subsections
7-11-2I, "Use Of Tobacco",
7-11-2S, "Consumption of Alcohol", and
7-11-2X, "Swimming/Beach Use", of this chapter, police officers or designees
shall enforce and be authorized to issue citation-complaints. Before issuing a
citation-complaint, the police officer or designee shall verify that the
offender has previously received a warning against engaging in such conduct, or
the offender has refused to discontinue engaging in such conduct after the
police officer or designee has advised the offender that such conduct must
cease. A one hundred dollar ($100.00) civil penalty shall be imposed for each
violation where a citation-complaint has been issued. For violations of
subsection
7-11-2C, "Parking", of this chapter, police officers or designees shall be
authorized to issue parking tickets as specified in title 6, "Motor Vehicles
And Traffic", of this code. (Ord. 2140, 3-21-2016; Ord. 2438, 9-8-2020)
CHAPTER 12
LIBRARY REGULATIONS
SECTION:
7-12-1: Purpose
7-12-2: Rules And Regulations
7-12-3: Violation; Penalty
7-12-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this chapter is to adopt certain library rules governing the
conduct of patrons of the library of the City. The term "library" as used
herein refers to the City Library Building located at 4000 Mills Civic Parkway,
West Des Moines, Iowa. (Ord. 1363, 5-17-1999)
7-12-2: RULES AND REGULATIONS:
The following rules and regulations are established concerning the conduct of
patrons and use of library facilities, as follows:
A.   Library patrons are expected to be engaged in the productive use of the
library's resources. This includes reading, studying, researching, attending
programs and utilizing library material. Patrons have the right to use the
library undisturbed and library employees have the right to work without undue
interference. Please note: Adult patrons in the children's or teen areas who
are not retrieving children's or teen materials nor are caregivers for a child
or teen may be asked to relocate to other areas of the library.
B.   The library will not tolerate bullying in any library space, gathering, or
program and staff will do all they reasonably can to create a safe space for
all library users, regardless of an individual's actual or perceived age,
color, creed/denomination, national origin, race, religion, marital status,
sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, physical attributes/appearance,
physical or mental ability or disability, ancestry, political party preference,
political belief, socioeconomic status, or familial status. Bullying is defined
as the unwanted, aggressive use of physical, social, or mental/intellectual
power to control, harm, or humiliate another person in a repetitive or
pervasive manner. All library users and employees should be free of any threat
of harm, invasion of property, or gross indignity.
C.   No person shall engage in any conduct which disturbs or interferes with
the legitimate use of the library, including - but not restricted to - the
following:
1.   Refuse to follow reasonable directives or instructions from a library
staff member.
2.   Willfully annoy, bully, harass, or threaten another person.
3.   Behave in a disorderly, loud, or boisterous manner, including loud
conversations.
4.   Interfere with another person's passage within the library or on library
grounds.
5.   Consume or possess alcoholic beverages unless the Library Board of
Trustees has approved of an event or function at the library where alcoholic
beverages will be provided. The consumption or possession of alcoholic
beverages shall be limited to that provided to those in attendance at the
approved library event or function, and shall be confined to a designated area
within the library during the event or function.
6.   Deface or destroy library property.
7.   Eat or drink(unless eating or drinking is specifically allowed in an area
or at a particular activity).
8.   Use tobacco or smoke in the library, including the use of electronic
cigarettes or vaping devices.
9.   Sleep in the library, or exhibit the appearance of sleep.
10.   Remain in the library after regular closing hours.
11.   Interfere with patrons' use of the library through poor bodily hygiene
which is so offensive as to constitute a nuisance, or through excessive use of
perfume, cologne, or alcohol.
12.   Bring animals into the library with the exception of service animals or
service-animals-in-training as defined by Title II and Title III of The
Americans with Disabilities Act and/or Iowa Code 216C.1A.
13.   Use sports equipment, skates, or a skateboard in the library.
14.   Use any audio, personal communication, or computing device in a manner
that is disturbing to other patrons. Cellphone ringers should be set to silent
or vibrate and device speakers muted or headphones used.
15.   Campaign, leaflet, petition, interview, or survey patrons or staff in a
manner that is disruptive to library activities.
16.   Willfully expose patrons and staff to offensive images or language.
17.   Engage in lengthy conversations (including conversations on cellphones)
in areas intended for quiet study.
18.   Interfere with the library's right to maintain a clean, pleasant, and
safe facility.
19.   Relocate or rearrange furniture beyond repositioning existing seating
around tables.
20.   Be in any state of inappropriate undress.
21.   Engage in sexual activity of any kind, including inappropriate displays
of romantic affection.
22.   Bring luggage, bedrolls, or large bags into the library.
23.   Leave packages, backpacks, or personal belongings unattended. Personal
property must be within sight of the owner. The library assumes no
responsibility for belongings left unattended.
24.   Use bathrooms for unreasonable or unintended purposes, such as bathing or
laundering.
D.   Patrons violating any of the above policies will have the matter called to
their attention once. Should the behavior continue, they will be asked to leave
the library facility and grounds. Should they refuse to leave, library staff
will contact the Director and the West Des Moines Police Department and the
patron(s) will be escorted from the premises. A refusal to leave after being
asked to leave by staff will be grounds for suspension of library privileges.
For minors, a suspension of privileges will be accompanied by an attempt-by
phone, email, or mail-to notify a parent or guardian. At the discretion of the
Library Director or Head of Youth Services, an attempt may be made to contact
the student and/or their caregiver via West Des Moines Community Schools. (Ord.
2321, 7-23-2018; amd. Ord. 2524, 6-20-2022)
7-12-3: VIOLATION; PENALTY:
Any person who violates the provisions of this chapter, upon conviction, shall
be punished not in excess of a one hundred dollar ($100.00) fine or in excess
of thirty (30) days' imprisonment. (Ord. 1363, 5-17-1999)
CHAPTER 13
SPECIAL ASSESSMENTS FOR STREETS
SECTION:
7-13-1: Purpose
7-13-2: Scope
7-13-3: Procedure
7-13-4: Payment Of Assessments
7-13-5: Agricultural Deferment
7-13-6: Deficiency Assessments
7-13-7: Assessment Methods
7-13-8: Benefits
7-13-9: Modified Flint Formula
7-13-10: Area (District) Assessment Method
7-13-11: Boundaries Of Assessment Districts For Area (District) Assessment
7-13-12: Methodology
7-13-1: PURPOSE:
A.   The purpose of this Chapter is to provide general guidance to staff and
notice to citizens concerning the processes utilized to establish special
assessments for street improvements which will be levied upon private property
in West Des Moines. Whenever the word "assessment" or words "special
assessment" are used in this Chapter, the word or words refer only to special
assessments for street improvement projects, including construction, paving,
reconstruction, resurfacing or repair measures.
B.   It is realized that special situations will arise which cannot be
anticipated in a general policy but which will need to be addressed in a
reasonable manner once they arise. While this Chapter cannot be literally
applied to every such exceptional situation, it is nonetheless the directive of
the City Council that the concepts reflected in this Chapter be fairly and
equitably applied in a reasonable fashion to all street assessments. (Ord.
1389, 10-4-1999)
7-13-2: SCOPE:
A.   Policy: It is the policy of the City to eventually have all streets within
the City paved or widened to the extent suitable to their intended or actual
use. All street improvement projects shall be assessed in accord with this
Chapter (as limited by the purpose) to the extent such improvement benefits
property in a definable benefited property district or area.
B.   Other Finance Mechanisms: The City Council recognizes that not all streets
are improved through use of a special assessment and that developers and others
may finance the improvement of streets through the use of other mechanisms.
Where such alternative mechanisms have effectively shifted costs to benefited
property owners, even when not formally assessed, such property owners shall be
treated as if their property had been previously assessed. The City will not
ordinarily place the same tract of land in more than one benefited property
district for assessment purposes.
C.   Street Width; Special Benefit: The amount assessed for any street
improvement project shall normally be equivalent to constructing, paving,
repairing, or widening a local street in accordance with the current Urban
Design Policy Standards Manual and the Urban Specifications for Construction of
Public Improvements (the "design standards") as adopted or amended by the City.
In so limiting the amount of assessment, it is the intent of the Council to
assess only for the special benefit derived from a street improvement project;
provided, however, that the City Council may in its discretion assess up to the
width of the classification of the street being improved, as provided in the
design standards.
D.   General Benefits: All general benefits from a street improvement project
in excess of the above standard shall be paid from other City funds and shall
not be assessed. Subject to final determination by the Council, the percentage
of general benefit to the City shall be determined in accordance with the
schedule set forth in subsection
7-13-3F of this Chapter.
E.   Assessable Items: Assessable items, to the extent special benefits are
conferred, shall include:
1.   All related storm sewer for the project (but not all storm sewer costs and
oversizing of drains necessitated by anticipated future expansion shall be
assessed).
2.   All required grading for the project.
3.   All utility relocations required due to the project.
4.   All driveways, sidewalks, and trails required due to the project.
5.   All surface restoration required by the project.
6.   All right of way required due to the project up to sixty feet (60').
7.   All the engineering fees associated with the design and construction of
the project.
8.   All legal fees associated with the project.
9.   All appraisal fees associated with the project.
10.   Pro rata share of administrative costs.
11.   Paving costs.
12.   Traffic signals where a special local benefit is conferred.
13.   All other miscellaneous costs and contingency costs directly related to
the project.
F.   Design Standards: All standards and details of design for proposed
assessment projects shall be in accordance with the design standards as amended
and the Comprehensive Plan as amended.
G.   Street Improvements: In addition to constructing new streets, the City may
assess for street widening, reconstruction, repair or resurfacing when such
improvement is found to confer special benefits. Such assessment will
ordinarily occur only in a manner consistent with this general statement, and
only to the extent that the property has not been assessed or owners have not
otherwise previously participated directly in the cost of such construction.
(Ord. 1389, 10-4-1999)
7-13-3: PROCEDURE:
A.   Procedural Steps: The City will generally endeavor to follow the
procedural steps set out in this Section.
B.   Identification Of Streets: City staff shall, during the budget process or
as part of the citizens Capital Improvement Program, and at other times as
directed by the City Council, identify streets which in the opinion of staff
should be considered for improvement. The City Manager shall review such
recommendations and report to the Mayor and City Council his or her findings as
to the need for improvement. The City Council shall act upon such
recommendations as part of its annual budgetary process, either through
consideration of capital improvement projects or at such times as may seem
proper in the circumstances.
C.   Petition By Property Owners: As an alternative, assessments for street
improvement projects may be initiated by petition of all property owners to be
assessed for the cost subject to Council approval. Such projects, however,
shall normally be considered in light of the regular budgetary process.
D.   Project Determination: After the initial considerations and discussions
set forth above, the City Council shall decide whether it wishes to consider a
street improvement project and whether that project should be specially
assessed. As part of such decision, the City Council shall direct the
appropriate eminent domain notice be issued, and may employ consulting
engineers, bond counsel and such other consultants as may be necessary.
E.   Preliminary Plat And Schedule Of Assessments: As part of the consideration
of whether to levy special assessment for a project, the City Council shall
direct the engineer to prepare a preliminary plat and schedule of assessments,
estimate the costs, and preliminary plans and specifications, and to furnish
necessary data to bond counsel needed to prepare legal proceedings. The
engineer shall present a preliminary draft of the plat and schedule to the City
staff which shall review the documents and make recommendations to the City
Council.
F.   Arterial Or Collector Streets: All streets classified in the then current
Comprehensive Plan as arterial or collector shall be considered to generally
benefit the community as well as specially benefited properties in the
benefited property district. Therefore, any reduction in the special assessment
shall generally be applied to the specially affected parcel within one hundred
fifty feet (150') of the street improvement project in accordance with the
following schedule:
 
Street Classification Amount Of Reduction
                      
Major arterial        40 percent
Minor arterial        20 percent
Major collector       10 percent
Minor collector       5 percent
 
The distance of one hundred fifty feet (150') on each side of the street shall
generally be applied to create an area similar to the area established by
application of the Flint Formula, as further set forth in Section
7-13-9 of this Chapter. The final determination of any reduction, however,
shall be established by the City Council.
G.   Property Valuation: The City Council shall determine the valuation of the
property to be specially assessed. The valuations for property within the
proposed assessment district shall not exceed the fair market value of the
property with the proposed public improvement in place. The City Council shall
retain the services of an MAI appraiser to advise the City Council as to its
findings regarding the valuation of each lot and parcel within the benefited
property district with the street improvement in place.
H.   Project Information Meeting: As part of the consideration of whether to
levy a special assessment for a street improvement project, the City Council
shall either conduct a project information meeting or direct staff to conduct a
project information meeting. Benefited property owners shall be notified by
letter with details concerning the proposed project and the time, location and
place of the meeting. Staff shall arrange for the delivery of the notification
at least ten (10) days prior to the meeting.
I.   Informational Pamphlet: Staff shall provide an informational pamphlet
describing the project, assessment procedure, and pertinent deadlines along
with a copy of this Chapter to those attending the project information meeting
and to others upon request. No official action shall be taken by the City
Council on the assessment proceeding within a thirty (30) day period following
the project information meeting to permit affected property owners to petition
for or against the project.
J.   Preliminary Plans And Specifications: At the completion of the above
process, the preliminary plans and specifications, preliminary plat, schedule
of assessments, and estimate of costs shall be officially filed in the office
of the City Clerk.
K.   Council Resolutions: After the filing of the preliminary plans and
specifications, preliminary plat, schedule of assessments, and estimate of
costs, the City Council shall meet to consider the preliminary resolution for
the street improvement project, resolution fixing value of lots, resolution
adopting preliminary plat and schedule, estimate of costs, and preliminary
plans and specifications. If the City Council adopts the foregoing, it shall
then consider a proposed resolution of necessity for the project and set a date
and time for public hearing on the proposed resolution of necessity.
L.   Notice To Property Owners; Publication: Notice shall then be given to the
affected property owners that the proposed resolution of necessity will be
considered by the City Council. The notice shall be published as required by
law.
M.   Resolution Of Necessity: The City Council shall hold a public hearing on
the resolution of necessity. The City Council shall hear all objections and
endorsements and consider all filed and written objections. The City Council
shall then officially continue or close the public hearing. After closing the
public hearing, the City Council may reject, adopt, or amend and adopt, the
proposed resolution of necessity, or the City Council may defer action until a
subsequent meeting.
N.   Required Vote: Passage of the resolution of necessity shall require the
affirmative vote of three-quarters (3/4) of the City Council; provided,
however, if written remonstrances signed by the owners of seventy five percent
(75%) of the amount of the proposed assessments on property subject to
assessment have been timely filed with the City Clerk, the resolution of
necessity will require the unanimous affirmative vote of the City Council for
passage.
O.   Plans And Specifications; Contract: If the resolution of necessity is
adopted either as proposed or as amended, the City Council shall then adopt
resolutions directing the preparation of detailed plans and specifications, and
the form of contract and notice to bidders.
P.   Court Decree: Following the adoption of either the original or amended
resolution of necessity when more than sixty percent (60%) of the amount of the
proposed assessments on property subject to assessment have petitioned against
the project, the City Council may direct bond counsel or other legal counsel to
file in District Court a petition requesting the Court to review and confirm
the proposed street improvement by decree. The City Council, at its own
discretion, retains the option of having other assessments for street projects
confirmed by the same process.
Q.   Detailed Plans And Specifications: Detailed plans and specifications and
the form of contract and notice to bidders shall officially be placed on file
in the City Clerk's office.
R.   Resolution Ordering Bids; Approving Plans: The City Council shall, either
at the meeting at which the resolution of necessity is adopted, or thereafter,
adopt a resolution ordering bids, approving plans, specifications and form of
contract, and notice to bidder; fixing amount of bid security; ordering City
Clerk to publish notice, fix a date for reviewing bids; and for a public
hearing on plans, specifications, form of contract and estimate of costs. The
notice to bidder shall then be published as required by law.
S.   Filing With County Treasurer: The resolution of necessity and preliminary
plat and schedule of assessments shall be filed in the county treasurer's
office as required by State law. The City Clerk shall also execute a
certificate with regard to the amount of agricultural deferment requests timely
filed by property owners pursuant to Section
7-13-5 of this Chapter.
T.   Public Hearing; Resolution Awarding Contract: The City Council shall hold
a public hearing on the plans, specifications, and form of contract as required
by the published notice. After the public hearing is complete, the Council may
adopt the resolution adopting plans, specifications, form of contract, and
estimated cost. Bids which have been received for the street improvement
project shall be evaluated by City staff and, where appropriate, consulting
engineers and legal counsel. If satisfactory bids have been received, the City
Council may adopt a resolution awarding a contract, or the City Council may
defer action, or for proper reasons reject all bids.
U.   Review Of Completed Work: After completion or substantial completion and
in accordance with law, the engineer shall review the completed work and file
certificates of completion and final estimates of costs with the City Clerk.
The total project cost and the total assessable cost of the project shall be
summarized by category with a full description of costs, including unit
quantities, available to the public on request.
V.   Resolution Accepting Work; Levy Of Final Assessments: The City Council
shall then adopt a resolution accepting the work and ordering preparation of
the final plat and schedule of assessments. The final plat and schedule of
assessment shall be filed by the engineer in the City Clerk's office. The
resolution adopting and levying the final assessments and providing for the
payment thereof shall then be adopted by the City Council. In no case may the
final assessments be greater than the preliminary assessment. Notice of filing
of the final plat and schedule shall be given as required by law.
W.   Final Plat And Schedule Filed With County Treasurer; Notice To Property
Owner: The City Clerk shall file a certificate of levy and copy of the final
plat and schedule in the office of the county treasurer and the Building Permit
Official's office. Notice of such filing shall be published for two (2)
consecutive weeks with the first publication not more than fifteen (15) days
from the date of filing the final plat and schedule with the county officials.
On or before the date of the second publication of notice, the Clerk shall
send, by ordinary and certified mail, a copy of the notice to each property
owner. (Ord. 1389, 10-4-1999)
7-13-4: PAYMENT OF ASSESSMENTS:
A.   Any assessment levied under this Chapter may be paid in full or in part
without interest within thirty (30) days after the date of certification.
B.   Except as to assessments of less than one hundred dollars ($100.00), which
must be paid in full before the next July 1, assessments may be paid, with
interest, in installments with real estate taxes over a period of ten (10)
years. (Ord. 1389, 10-4-1999)
7-13-5: AGRICULTURAL DEFERMENT:
A.   Persons having a tract of land, either alone or as an integral part of a
larger tract, which is both used and assessed for agricultural purposes, and
which would otherwise be subject to assessment, may apply for an agricultural
deferment as provided by State law.
B.   Any property owner who seeks deferment of an assessment shall file a
written request for deferment with the City Clerk at the time of the hearing on
the resolution of necessity or within ten (10) days following the date of the
closing of the public hearing. The request shall identify those lots subject to
the proposed assessment which the property owner claims are entitled to
agricultural deferment.
C.   It shall be the responsibility of the property owner to make such
additional annual filings as are required by law for the continuation of an
agricultural deferment. (Ord. 1389, 10-4-1999)
7-13-6: DEFICIENCY ASSESSMENTS:
A.   If the proposed assessment is greater than twenty five percent (25%) of
the value of any tract with the improvement in place, the Council shall provide
by resolution that the portion of the assessment which exceeds twenty five
percent (25%) of the value of the tract with the improvement in place shall be
certified to the county treasurer as a deficiency.
B.   The amount of the deficiency shall amortize over a period of ten (10)
years and after ten (10) years no part of the deficiency may be assessed;
provided, however, that if a private improvement is constructed on a lot
subject to deficiency during the period of amortization, the pro-rata
deficiency on the lot which has not been amortized shall be assessed to the
extent that it is assessable. (Ord. 1389, 10-4-1999)
7-13-7: ASSESSMENT METHODS:
A.   The City Council has elected to use formulas as a guide to the exercise of
its legislative power to determine the proper amount to be assessed against
property which receives a special benefit from a street improvement project.
Depending upon the character of the street to be improved, the City will
utilize a method of assessment which assures that the assessable costs of a
street improvement project are fairly spread among benefited properties and
that no property is assessed an amount greater than the special benefit
received.
B.   In its sole legislative discretion, the City Council shall determine
whether the application and use of a formula to guide it in establishing the
amount of individual assessments meet the criteria established by this Chapter
and the law. (Ord. 1389, 10-4-1999)
7-13-8: BENEFITS:
A.   Benefit Conferred: It is the policy of the City not to assess any amount
for street improvements in excess of the benefit conferred on a lot or parcel.
Benefits resulting from street improvements which inure to property owners
within the assessment area will depend upon the circumstances of each project.
B.   Nature And Extent Of Benefits: As a result of street improvement projects,
property owners often benefit from enhanced access, an improved environment
because of dust and drainage control, enhancement of aesthetic qualities in the
area, a decrease in the cost of automobile and other vehicle maintenance, an
improvement in the ability of police, fire, ambulance and other public safety
organizations to respond, an increase in the value of property, and an
improvement in the ability of property owners to market their property either
